tactics.name: Surveillance & Tracking
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to monitor the victim's location, activities, communications, and relationships without consent or beyond consent given. Surveillance techniques enable perpetrators to maintain awareness of victim movements, predict behavior, and gather information for use in other tactics.

tactics.name: Account & Access Compromise
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gain unauthorized access to victim's accounts, devices, or digital identity, or deny victim access to their own. These techniques enable perpetrators to control victim's digital presence, access private information, and restrict victim's autonomy.

tactics.name: Harassment & Intimidation
tactics.description: The adversary is directly threatening, frightening, humiliating, or exhausting victim through digital means. These techniques create fear, emotional distress, and psychological harm through sustained digital aggression.

tactics.name: Information Manipulation
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to control, distort, fabricate, or weaponize information to harm victim's reality, reputation, or relationships. These techniques undermine victim's credibility, social support, and sense of reality.

tactics.name: Isolation & Control
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to cut victim off from support networks, control their communications, or restrict their digital autonomy. These techniques reduce victim's ability to seek help, maintain relationships, or exercise independent judgment.

tactics.name: Resource & Financial Control
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to control, restrict, or exploit victim's financial resources and economic independence through technology. These techniques create financial dependency, economic harm, and material vulnerability.

tactics.name: Physical Enablement
tactics.description: The adversary is using technology to enable, coordinate, or amplify physical-world harm. These techniques bridge digital abuse to physical danger, representing the most severe escalation of tech-facilitated abuse.

tactics.name: Grooming & Targeted Recruitment
tactics.description: Techniques for building exploitative relationships via technology. Covers child grooming, romance fraud initiation, and trafficking recruitment. The perpetrator uses technology to identify, approach, build trust with, desensitise, and ultimately exploit a target.
tactics.public_intro: These are ways someone might use technology to build a relationship with you (or your child) specifically to exploit, control, or harm you later. It often starts with flattery, attention, and gifts — and gradually crosses boundaries.
tactics.public_safety: If you or your child is being contacted by someone who seems 'too good to be true' — especially if they're pushing for private communication, asking personal questions quickly, or making you feel obligated — trust that instinct. Contact 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or, for children, Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800).

tactics.name: Discovery & Preparation
tactics.description: How perpetrators learn, discover, and acquire the tools and techniques for technology-facilitated abuse. The pre-attack phase — understanding where someone learns to install stalkerware, discovers AirTag tracking, or is recruited into scam operations. Prevention-focused tactic for NFPs, law enforcement, and educators.
tactics.public_name: How People Learn to Do This
tactics.public_intro: Understanding where and how people learn abusive techniques helps us prevent harm before it starts. These patterns show how surveillance tools are normalised, how controlling behaviours are taught, and where intervention is most effective.
tactics.public_safety: If you recognise these patterns in someone you know — or in yourself — support is available. Reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. Contact 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732).

techniques.name: Stalkerware Installation
techniques.description: Installing hidden monitoring software on victim's device to track location, messages, calls, photos, and keystrokes. Stalkerware (also called spouseware or creepware) is commercially available software marketed for 'parental monitoring' or 'employee tracking' but frequently used for intimate partner surveillance. These apps typically hide their presence, run silently in the background, and transmit data to the perpetrator.
techniques.public_summary: Someone installs a hidden app on your phone or computer that secretly tracks your location, reads your messages, and monitors your calls — without anything visible on screen.
techniques.safety_warning: If you think there's a monitoring app on your phone, don't remove it straight away. The person who installed it may be alerted and could become dangerous. Get advice from a specialist service first.

notices.signal: Your phone battery is draining much faster than usual
notices.detail: Monitoring apps run constantly in the background, which uses a lot of battery power.

notices.signal: You're using more mobile data than expected
notices.detail: The app sends your information to the other person, which uses data — even when you're not actively using your phone.

notices.signal: Your phone feels warm even when you're not using it
notices.detail: Background monitoring processes generate heat.

notices.signal: The other person seems to know things they shouldn't
notices.detail: They mention details from your private messages, know where you've been, or reference conversations they weren't part of.

notices.signal: You notice unfamiliar apps or settings on your device
notices.detail: Look for apps you don't recognise, or device administrator settings you didn't set up.

actions.action: Use a stalkerware detection app to check your phone
actions.detail: Apps like those recommended by the Coalition Against Stalkerware can scan for known monitoring software.
actions.safety_note: Running a scan is generally safe — the monitoring person typically can't see that you've installed a detection app.

actions.action: Keep your phone locked with a PIN or biometric
actions.detail: Use a strong passcode that the other person doesn't know. Avoid patterns that are easy to watch and copy.

actions.action: Consider getting a separate safe phone
actions.detail: A prepaid phone the other person doesn't know about can be used for sensitive calls and messages.
actions.safety_note: Keep it hidden and don't connect it to any accounts the other person knows about.

actions.action: Keep your phone's software up to date
actions.detail: Updates fix security holes that monitoring apps exploit.

actions.action: Get a professional to examine your device
actions.detail: A digital forensic specialist can find hidden monitoring software and preserve evidence.
actions.safety_note: Ask a support service for referrals — don't search for this on a monitored device.

mitigations.name: Anti-Stalkerware Scanning
mitigations.description: Deploy anti-stalkerware detection tools to identify monitoring applications. Scan for apps with excessive permissions including location, microphone, camera, and message access.

mitigations.name: Device Access Controls
mitigations.description: Implement strong device authentication. Disable installation from unknown sources. Maintain physical control of devices.

mitigations.name: Safe Device Acquisition
mitigations.description: Obtain a separate device for sensitive communications if stalkerware is suspected. Removing stalkerware may alert the monitoring party.

mitigations.name: Operating System Hardening
mitigations.description: Maintain current OS versions. Security updates frequently patch vulnerabilities exploited by stalkerware.

mitigations.name: Forensic Device Audit
mitigations.description: Engage professional forensic analysis to identify monitoring software and preserve evidence.

detections.name: Anomalous Battery Consumption
detections.description: Device battery depletes faster than baseline due to continuous background data transmission.

detections.name: Unexplained Data Usage
detections.description: Increased mobile data consumption without corresponding user activity. Monitor per-app data usage for unknown processes.

detections.name: Device Temperature Anomalies
detections.description: Device runs hot during idle periods indicating background process activity.

detections.name: Information Leakage Indicators
detections.description: Adversary demonstrates knowledge of private communications, locations, or activities accessible only through device monitoring.

detections.name: Unknown Applications or Profiles
detections.description: Presence of unrecognised apps, device administrator privileges, or configuration profiles.

sub_techniques.name: Commercial Stalkerware (mSpy, FlexiSpy, etc.)
sub_techniques.description: Installation of commercially available stalkerware products specifically marketed for monitoring. Products like mSpy, FlexiSpy, Cocospy, and Spyic offer subscription-based phone monitoring with features including message reading, call recording, location tracking, and keylogging.
sub_techniques.public_title: Commercial spy apps installed on your phone
sub_techniques.public_summary: Products like mSpy or FlexiSpy are sold online as monitoring tools. Someone may have installed one on your phone — these apps hide themselves and send everything you do to another person.

notices.signal: You find an unfamiliar app with a generic name like 'System Service' or 'Update Service'
notices.detail: Stalkerware apps disguise themselves with boring names so you won't notice them.

actions.action: Use a stalkerware detection tool
actions.detail: The Coalition Against Stalkerware recommends specific detection apps. Visit stopstalkerware.org for guidance.
actions.safety_note: Get safety advice before removing — the person may be alerted.

sub_techniques.name: Dual-Use Parental Control Abuse
sub_techniques.description: Repurposing legitimate parental control apps (Qustodio, Bark, Google Family Link, Apple Screen Time) for adult partner surveillance. These apps are designed for child safety but provide comprehensive monitoring when applied to an adult's device.
sub_techniques.public_title: Parental control apps used to monitor an adult
sub_techniques.public_summary: Apps designed to keep children safe — like Google Family Link or Screen Time — can also be used to monitor and control an adult partner's phone usage, location, and communications.

notices.signal: Your phone has restrictions you didn't set
notices.detail: App limits, content filters, or screen time restrictions that you didn't configure — someone with admin access set these up.

actions.action: Check for device administrator or Family accounts
actions.detail: On Android: Settings > Security > Device Admin. On iPhone: Settings > Screen Time. If someone else's account controls yours, that's not normal.

sub_techniques.name: Enterprise MDM Stalkerware
sub_techniques.description: Using enterprise mobile device management (MDM) tools for intimate partner monitoring. MDM profiles can be installed that provide comprehensive device control including location tracking, app management, message access, and remote wipe capability.
sub_techniques.public_title: Work-style device management used to control your phone
sub_techniques.public_summary: Your phone may have a management profile installed — the kind normally used by employers — that gives another person control over your device, access to your location, and the ability to read your data.

notices.signal: Your phone shows 'This device is managed' or similar
notices.detail: On iPhone: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management. On Android: Settings > Security > Device Admin.

actions.action: Check for MDM profiles
actions.detail: If you find a management profile you didn't install, get advice before removing it — the administrator will be notified.
actions.safety_note: Seek specialist tech safety advice from eSafety Commissioner.

sub_techniques.name: Accessibility Service Abuse
sub_techniques.description: Android stalkerware that uses the Accessibility Service API to read screen content from any app, including encrypted messengers like Signal and WhatsApp. This technique defeats end-to-end encryption because it reads the screen after decryption. The stalkerware reads what's displayed, not the network traffic.
sub_techniques.public_title: Spy software that reads your screen — even encrypted messages
sub_techniques.public_summary: Some monitoring apps use a special Android feature called 'Accessibility Services' to read everything displayed on your screen — including messages in Signal, WhatsApp, and other encrypted apps. Encryption doesn't help because the app reads what's on screen, not what's sent over the network.

notices.signal: They know the content of your Signal or WhatsApp messages
notices.detail: If someone knows what you wrote in an encrypted app, screen-reading software is a likely explanation.

actions.action: Check Accessibility Services on Android
actions.detail: Settings > Accessibility. If an unfamiliar app has accessibility access, it may be reading your screen.
actions.safety_note: Get specialist advice before disabling — the monitoring person may be alerted.

techniques.name: Physical Tracker Planting
techniques.description: Placing GPS tracking devices such as AirTags, Tile trackers, or vehicle GPS units in victim's belongings, vehicle, or on their person without consent. These commercially available devices are inexpensive, small, and designed for long battery life, making covert placement easy. Perpetrators use them to monitor victim's movements, identify frequented locations, and anticipate travel patterns.
techniques.public_summary: Someone places a small tracking device — like an AirTag, Tile, or GPS tracker — in your bag, car, or belongings to follow your movements.
techniques.safety_warning: If you find a tracker, think carefully before removing it. Removing it tells the other person you found it. Document it first (photo with date) and get advice.

notices.signal: Your phone alerts you about an unknown tracker travelling with you
notices.detail: iPhones and some Android phones will warn you if an unknown AirTag or similar device is nearby for a long time.

notices.signal: The other person always seems to know where you are
notices.detail: They reference specific places you've been, your routes, or when you arrived somewhere — without you telling them.

notices.signal: You find a small unfamiliar device in your things
notices.detail: Trackers can be small — about the size of a coin. Check under seats, in wheel wells, inside bag pockets, or attached to keyrings.

notices.signal: You hear periodic beeping from your bag or car
notices.detail: Some trackers beep to help owners find them. If you hear unexplained beeping, investigate.

actions.action: Enable unknown tracker alerts on your phone
actions.detail: On iPhone, this is on by default. Android users can download the Tracker Detect app or enable similar built-in features.

actions.action: Check your car systematically
actions.detail: Look under the chassis, in wheel wells, behind bumpers, in the boot, and under seats. A torch and mirror help.

actions.action: Check your everyday bags and belongings
actions.detail: Go through pockets, linings, and any compartments. Feel for small hard objects that shouldn't be there.

actions.action: Document before removing
actions.detail: If you find a tracker, photograph it in place with a timestamp. This preserves evidence.
actions.safety_note: Consider whether it's safer to leave it in place temporarily while you make a safety plan.

mitigations.name: Bluetooth Tracker Detection
mitigations.description: Use tracker detection applications to scan for nearby Bluetooth tracking devices. Enable platform-native unknown tracker alerts.

mitigations.name: Physical Vehicle Inspection
mitigations.description: Conduct systematic inspection of vehicles for GPS tracking devices in common concealment locations.

mitigations.name: Belongings Audit
mitigations.description: Inspect bags, clothing, and frequently carried items for concealed tracking devices.

mitigations.name: Evidence Preservation Protocol
mitigations.description: If tracker discovered, document location and preserve for evidence before removal. Removal alerts monitoring party.

detections.name: Platform Tracker Alerts
detections.description: Device displays alerts for unknown tracking devices travelling with user.

detections.name: Location Knowledge Indicators
detections.description: Adversary references specific locations, routes, or timing not disclosed by target.

detections.name: Physical Device Discovery
detections.description: Small electronic device found attached to vehicle or concealed in belongings.

detections.name: Audible Tracker Indicators
detections.description: Periodic beeping from unknown source in belongings or vehicle.

sub_techniques.name: AirTag / SmartTag Planting
sub_techniques.description: Hiding Apple AirTags, Samsung SmartTags, or Tile trackers in bags, vehicles, clothing pockets, or children's belongings to track location. Consumer Bluetooth trackers are cheap, small, and easy to hide.
sub_techniques.public_title: A small tracking device hidden in your belongings
sub_techniques.public_summary: Apple AirTags, Samsung SmartTags, and Tile trackers are small enough to hide in a bag, car, or coat pocket. Someone may have placed one in your belongings to track your location.

notices.signal: Your iPhone alerts you to an 'AirTag Found Moving With You'
notices.detail: Apple sends alerts when an unknown AirTag is travelling with you. Take this seriously.

notices.signal: You find a small disc-shaped device you don't recognise
notices.detail: AirTags are coin-sized white discs. SmartTags are similar. Check bags, car compartments, and jacket pockets.

actions.action: If you find an unknown tracker, don't destroy it
actions.detail: It may contain evidence. Keep it and report to police. You can disable an AirTag by removing the battery.
actions.safety_note: Consider that removing the tracker may alert the person tracking you.

actions.action: Android users: install Apple's Tracker Detect app or use Bluetooth scanner
actions.detail: Android doesn't automatically alert for AirTags. Install a detection app.

sub_techniques.name: Vehicle GPS Tracker Installation
sub_techniques.description: Installing dedicated GPS tracking devices in a vehicle's OBD-II port, under the chassis (magnetic mount), in wheel wells, or hardwired into vehicle electronics. Dedicated vehicle trackers can be harder to detect than consumer Bluetooth trackers and don't trigger phone alerts.
sub_techniques.public_title: A GPS tracker hidden in your car
sub_techniques.public_summary: A GPS tracking device may be hidden in your car — under the chassis, in the diagnostic port, or wired into the electronics. These are harder to find than AirTags and your phone won't alert you.

notices.signal: Someone always seems to know where you've driven
notices.detail: If they reference specific locations, routes, or stops without explanation, a vehicle tracker is possible.

actions.action: Have a mechanic check your vehicle
actions.detail: Ask them to check the OBD-II port (under the dashboard), wheel wells, and undercarriage for attached devices.
actions.safety_note: Use a trusted mechanic the other person doesn't know about.

sub_techniques.name: Find My / Google Find My Device Misuse
sub_techniques.description: Exploiting Apple Find My or Google Find My Device through shared family accounts, left-behind devices, or compromised credentials to track location in real time. Uses legitimate platform features — harder to classify as 'stalkerware' because it's built into the operating system.
sub_techniques.public_title: Being tracked through Find My iPhone or Google
sub_techniques.public_summary: If someone has access to your Apple ID or Google account, they can see your real-time location through Find My iPhone or Google Find My Device — without installing anything on your phone.

notices.signal: You're still on a shared Apple Family or Google Family plan with the other person
notices.detail: Family sharing often includes location sharing by default.

actions.action: Leave shared family plans and change account passwords
actions.detail: Remove yourself from Family Sharing (Apple) or Family Link (Google) and change your password.
actions.safety_note: Plan your digital safety steps with a specialist first — sudden changes may be noticed.

techniques.name: Shared Account Surveillance
techniques.description: Exploiting legitimately shared accounts or location sharing services (Find My Friends, Google location sharing, family phone plans) to monitor victim beyond the scope of original consent. Often occurs in relationships where sharing was mutual but continues after separation, or where the perpetrator coerces ongoing access under the guise of reasonable family coordination.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses accounts you share — like a family phone plan, streaming service, or cloud storage — to track your location, purchases, or activity.
techniques.safety_warning: Changing shared account settings may alert the other person. Plan which accounts to separate first and do them in a safe order.

notices.signal: The other person knows about purchases, locations, or content you haven't shared
notices.detail: Shared accounts like Google, Apple Family, or phone plans often show activity to all members.

notices.signal: You discover location sharing is turned on with their account
notices.detail: Check your phone's location sharing settings — someone may have enabled sharing without you realising.

notices.signal: Unfamiliar devices appear in your account's trusted devices list
notices.detail: Someone else's phone or computer may be logged into your shared accounts.

actions.action: Review all location sharing settings on your devices
actions.detail: On iPhone: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > Share My Location. On Android: Google Maps > your profile > Location sharing.

actions.action: Gradually move to your own individual accounts
actions.detail: Create new accounts with a fresh email address the other person doesn't know about.
actions.safety_note: Do this from a device and network you're confident isn't monitored.

actions.action: Check your phone plan
actions.detail: Family plans often let the account holder see call logs, texts, and data usage for all lines.
actions.safety_note: Moving to your own plan is ideal, but timing matters — plan it.

mitigations.name: Location Sharing Audit
mitigations.description: Review all location sharing configurations across devices and services. Disable unauthorised sharing.

mitigations.name: Account Separation
mitigations.description: Migrate to individual accounts for services previously shared. Use new credentials unknown to adversary.

mitigations.name: Carrier Account Review
mitigations.description: Assess family phone plan features that expose location or usage data. Plan migration to individual account.

detections.name: Shared Account Data References
detections.description: Adversary references location, purchases, or activities visible through shared account access.

detections.name: Active Location Sharing Discovery
detections.description: Audit reveals location sharing enabled with adversary's account.

detections.name: Unknown Devices on Shared Accounts
detections.description: Unrecognised devices listed in shared account trusted device lists.

techniques.name: Social Media Monitoring
techniques.description: Systematic observation of victim's public and semi-public social media activity, connections, check-ins, likes, comments, and tagged posts. May include creating fake accounts to follow private profiles, monitoring friends' posts for references to victim, or using social media analytics tools to track patterns of activity and connections.
techniques.public_summary: Someone closely monitors your social media accounts — tracking your posts, checking who you interact with, and using your activity to keep tabs on your life.

notices.signal: The other person comments on things you posted but didn't tell them about
notices.detail: They reference photos, check-ins, or interactions they saw on your social media.

notices.signal: You notice unfamiliar accounts following you or viewing your stories
notices.detail: They may have created fake accounts to watch you even after being blocked.

notices.signal: Friends mention the other person asking about your posts
notices.detail: They may be monitoring through mutual contacts.

actions.action: Tighten your privacy settings on every platform
actions.detail: Set profiles to private. Review who can see your posts, stories, friends list, and tagged photos.

actions.action: Review and clean up your followers and connections
actions.detail: Remove accounts you don't recognise or that seem suspicious.

actions.action: Stop posting real-time locations or future plans
actions.detail: Share holiday photos after you're home. Don't tag your current location.

actions.action: Turn off tagging or require approval for tags
actions.detail: This prevents friends from accidentally revealing your location through their posts.

mitigations.name: Privacy Configuration Hardening
mitigations.description: Configure maximum privacy settings on all social media platforms. Restrict visibility of posts, connections, and activity.

mitigations.name: Connection Audit
mitigations.description: Review all followers and connections for adversary-controlled accounts. Remove suspicious connections.

mitigations.name: Information Disclosure Controls
mitigations.description: Avoid posting real-time locations, routines, or future plans. Delay posting until after events conclude.

mitigations.name: Tag and Mention Restrictions
mitigations.description: Disable or require approval for tags and mentions to prevent third-party location disclosure.

detections.name: Non-Public Activity Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary references social media activity that should not be visible given current privacy settings.

detections.name: Suspicious Account Patterns
detections.description: New follower accounts created recently with minimal activity or connections to adversary's network.

detections.name: Third-Party Monitoring Reports
detections.description: Contacts report adversary has shown them target's social media content or asked about online activity.

techniques.name: Communication Interception
techniques.description: Accessing victim's emails, text messages, voicemails, and other communications through compromised accounts, email forwarding rules, message mirroring, or linked devices. Perpetrator reads, copies, or monitors communications without victim's knowledge, gaining intelligence about victim's plans, support network, and emotional state.
techniques.public_summary: Someone intercepts and reads your private messages, emails, or calls — either by accessing your accounts directly or by using software that copies your communications.
techniques.safety_warning: If your communications are being intercepted, the other person can see your safety planning. Use a different device or in-person conversations for sensitive discussions.

notices.signal: Messages show as 'read' before you've opened them
notices.detail: Someone else may be accessing your messaging accounts.

notices.signal: The other person responds to things said in private conversations
notices.detail: They reference details from messages or calls you had with other people.

notices.signal: Email forwarding rules you didn't set up
notices.detail: Check your email settings for auto-forwarding to unknown addresses.

notices.signal: Unfamiliar devices in your account's active sessions
notices.detail: Most email and messaging services show which devices are currently logged in.

actions.action: Check active sessions on all your accounts
actions.detail: Gmail: Security > Your devices. Facebook: Settings > Security > Where you're logged in. Do this for all platforms.

actions.action: Check for email forwarding rules
actions.detail: In Gmail: Settings > Forwarding. In Outlook: Settings > Mail > Forwarding. Remove anything you didn't set up.

actions.action: Use end-to-end encrypted messaging for sensitive conversations
actions.detail: Apps like Signal encrypt messages so only you and the recipient can read them.
actions.safety_note: Only useful if your device itself isn't compromised.

actions.action: Change passwords from a safe device
actions.detail: Use a device the other person hasn't had access to.
actions.safety_note: A trusted friend's phone or a library computer can work.

mitigations.name: Email Rule Audit
mitigations.description: Check email settings for unauthorised forwarding rules and filters. Remove rules forwarding to unknown addresses.

mitigations.name: Linked Device Review
mitigations.description: Review and remove unrecognised devices linked to messaging accounts.

mitigations.name: Encrypted Communications
mitigations.description: Use end-to-end encrypted messaging for sensitive communications. Ensure adversary cannot access linked devices.

mitigations.name: Voicemail Security
mitigations.description: Change voicemail PIN. Disable remote voicemail access where possible.

detections.name: Read Receipt Anomalies
detections.description: Messages marked as read before target has viewed them. Account shows online status during non-use periods.

detections.name: Unauthorised Forwarding Rules
detections.description: Email settings contain forwarding rules to unknown addresses or filters moving messages automatically.

detections.name: Unknown Linked Devices
detections.description: Messaging app settings show unrecognised devices with active sessions.

detections.name: Communication Content Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary quotes or references private message content.

techniques.name: Smart Home Surveillance
techniques.description: Using shared smart home devices including cameras, video doorbells, baby monitors, voice assistants, and other IoT devices to monitor victim's presence, activities, conversations, and visitors. Often exploits devices installed during cohabitation where perpetrator retains administrative access after separation.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses smart home devices — cameras, doorbells, speakers, or home assistants — to watch, listen to, or record you in your own home.
techniques.safety_warning: Smart home devices are often controlled by whoever set up the account. If you're in a shared home, the other person may have admin access to all devices.

notices.signal: Smart home devices behave unexpectedly
notices.detail: Cameras move on their own, speakers activate without prompts, or lights/locks change without your input.

notices.signal: The other person knows what's happening inside the home
notices.detail: They reference private conversations or activities that happened when they weren't present.

notices.signal: You can't control devices or change settings
notices.detail: You don't have admin access, or settings keep reverting after you change them.

notices.signal: Indicator lights on cameras or devices activate at odd times
notices.detail: Small LED lights on cameras may blink when recording or being accessed remotely.

actions.action: Check which accounts control your smart home devices
actions.detail: Identify who has admin access to cameras, speakers, locks, and thermostats.

actions.action: Physically disconnect devices you're concerned about
actions.detail: Unplug cameras and smart speakers. Cover camera lenses with tape if you can't unplug.
actions.safety_note: The other person may notice if devices go offline.

actions.action: Change Wi-Fi passwords
actions.detail: This disconnects all devices. You can then selectively reconnect only the ones you control.
actions.safety_note: Only do this if you safely control the router.

actions.action: Do a factory reset on devices you want to keep
actions.detail: This removes previous account connections. Set them up fresh with your own account.

mitigations.name: Smart Home Account Takeover
mitigations.description: Transfer device ownership to sole-controlled account. Factory reset devices and reconfigure with new credentials.

mitigations.name: Recording Device Audit
mitigations.description: Identify all cameras, microphones, and recording-capable devices. Disable or remove devices that cannot be secured.

mitigations.name: Voice Assistant Hardening
mitigations.description: Disable remote access features, drop-in capabilities, and voice purchasing. Delete stored recordings.

detections.name: In-Home Activity Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary references conversations or activities that occurred inside the home.

detections.name: Device Behaviour Anomalies
detections.description: Cameras activating, indicator lights engaging, or voice assistants responding without user trigger.

detections.name: Unauthorised Device Access
detections.description: Smart home app settings show adversary account retains admin or viewer access.

techniques.name: Network Traffic Monitoring
techniques.description: Monitoring victim's internet activity through router administrative access, DNS logs, or network monitoring tools. Perpetrator can see websites visited, search queries, app usage patterns, and connected devices. May install network-level monitoring tools or exploit existing router features.
techniques.public_summary: Someone monitors your internet traffic through the home router or network — seeing which websites you visit, what you search for, and what services you use.
techniques.safety_warning: If someone controls the home network, they may be able to see your browsing activity. Use mobile data instead of Wi-Fi for sensitive searches.

notices.signal: The other person knows what you've been searching or browsing
notices.detail: They reference websites you visited or things you looked up.

notices.signal: Unfamiliar software on the router or network
notices.detail: Network monitoring tools or DNS logging may have been enabled.

notices.signal: Your internet seems slower than expected
notices.detail: Monitoring tools can slightly slow down network traffic.

actions.action: Use your mobile data for sensitive browsing
actions.detail: Switch off Wi-Fi and use 4G/5G when searching for support services, legal help, or safety planning.

actions.action: Use a VPN on your devices
actions.detail: A VPN encrypts your internet traffic so it can't be read by someone monitoring the network.
actions.safety_note: The other person may notice a VPN is installed on your device.

actions.action: Check your router's settings
actions.detail: Look for logging, monitoring, or DNS filtering features that may have been enabled.
actions.safety_note: Only access router settings if you're confident the other person won't notice.

mitigations.name: Router Credential Reset
mitigations.description: Change router admin credentials. Factory reset router if adversary configured it.

mitigations.name: Traffic Encryption
mitigations.description: Use VPN to encrypt internet traffic and prevent network-level monitoring.

mitigations.name: Network Bypass
mitigations.description: Use mobile data instead of home network for sensitive browsing.

detections.name: Browsing Activity Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary references websites visited or searches performed.

detections.name: Unauthorised Network Controls
detections.description: Router contains parental controls, content filtering, or logging not configured by target.

detections.name: Network Monitoring Tools Present
detections.description: Discovery of network monitoring software or devices on home network.

techniques.name: Calendar/Schedule Surveillance
techniques.description: Accessing victim's calendar applications, booking systems, medical appointment portals, or work schedules to track movements and anticipate whereabouts. May exploit shared family calendars, compromised account access, or work systems to build a detailed picture of victim's routine.
techniques.public_summary: Someone monitors your calendar, schedule, or booking apps to know where you'll be and when — including appointments, meetings, and social plans.

notices.signal: The other person shows up at events or appointments they shouldn't know about
notices.detail: They appear at places you only noted in your calendar.

notices.signal: They reference your schedule without you telling them
notices.detail: They mention meetings, appointments, or plans from your calendar.

notices.signal: Your calendar is shared with accounts you don't recognise
notices.detail: Check calendar sharing settings for unexpected connections.

actions.action: Review calendar sharing settings
actions.detail: In Google Calendar: Settings > each calendar > Share with specific people. Remove anyone unexpected.

actions.action: Keep a separate private calendar
actions.detail: Use a different app or account for sensitive appointments — support services, legal consultations, etc.

actions.action: Check which apps have access to your calendar
actions.detail: On your phone: Settings > Privacy > Calendar. Remove access for apps that don't need it.

mitigations.name: Calendar Sharing Audit
mitigations.description: Review and remove unauthorised calendar sharing permissions across all calendar applications.

mitigations.name: Sensitive Appointment Isolation
mitigations.description: Use separate calendar on adversary-unknown account for sensitive appointments.

mitigations.name: Medical Portal Security
mitigations.description: Change credentials on health portals. Remove adversary as authorised contact.

detections.name: Appointment Interception
detections.description: Adversary appears at calendar events they should not know about.

detections.name: Schedule Knowledge Indicators
detections.description: Adversary references upcoming appointments before disclosure.

detections.name: Active Calendar Sharing
detections.description: Audit reveals adversary retains calendar viewing access.

techniques.name: Third-Party Monitoring Recruitment
techniques.description: Enlisting friends, family members, mutual contacts, or acquaintances (sometimes called 'flying monkeys') to monitor and report on victim's activities, location, companions, and emotional state. May involve deliberately maintaining relationships with victim's contacts for intelligence gathering purposes.
techniques.public_summary: Someone convinces friends, family, neighbours, or mutual contacts to report back on your activities, either openly or without you knowing.

notices.signal: Information you only shared with specific people gets back to the other person
notices.detail: Things you told a friend in confidence are known to someone who shouldn't know.

notices.signal: Mutual contacts ask unusually detailed questions
notices.detail: People start asking where you're going, who you're seeing, or what your plans are — more than feels natural.

notices.signal: You notice people watching or checking on you
notices.detail: Neighbours, work colleagues, or acquaintances seem to be tracking your comings and goings.

actions.action: Be thoughtful about what you share and with whom
actions.detail: Consider which contacts might pass information to the other person, even without bad intent.

actions.action: Create an inner circle of trusted people
actions.detail: Identify a small number of people you trust completely and keep sensitive information within that circle.

actions.action: Have a conversation with people you suspect are reporting back
actions.detail: Sometimes people don't realise they're being used. A calm conversation may help.

mitigations.name: Information Compartmentalisation
mitigations.description: Limit sensitive information shared with contacts who maintain relationship with adversary.

mitigations.name: Network Trust Assessment
mitigations.description: Identify which contacts may relay information to adversary based on information leakage patterns.

mitigations.name: Canary Information Testing
mitigations.description: Share unique details with specific contacts to identify information relay sources.

detections.name: Source-Specific Information Leakage
detections.description: Adversary gains knowledge of information shared only with specific individuals.

detections.name: Unusual Contact Questioning
detections.description: Contacts ask unusually specific questions about location, plans, or relationships.

detections.name: Recruitment Attempt Reports
detections.description: Trusted contacts report adversary has requested information about target.

techniques.name: Fitness/Health Tracker Surveillance
techniques.description: Monitoring victim through health and fitness applications, wearable trackers, period tracking apps, sleep monitors, or medical portals. These platforms often contain highly sensitive data about location, physical activity, health conditions, reproductive status, and daily routines.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses fitness trackers, health apps, or wearable devices to monitor your location, activity patterns, sleep, and health data.

notices.signal: The other person knows about your exercise routes or activity patterns
notices.detail: They reference when and where you exercised, or your daily routine.

notices.signal: Health or fitness data is being shared with their account
notices.detail: Shared fitness challenges, family health accounts, or linked apps may expose your data.

notices.signal: Your wearable shows locations or activity you didn't do
notices.detail: Someone else may be accessing and viewing your tracker data remotely.

actions.action: Review sharing settings on fitness and health apps
actions.detail: Check Fitbit, Apple Health, Strava, Garmin, and similar apps for shared access or linked accounts.

actions.action: Remove exercise routes from public or shared view
actions.detail: Many fitness apps share routes by default. Switch to private or remove location from activities.

actions.action: Check who has access to your health data
actions.detail: Apple Health: Settings > Health > Data Access. Google Fit: account settings > connected apps.

mitigations.name: Health Account Separation
mitigations.description: Unlink health and fitness accounts from shared or adversary-known accounts. Create new accounts with private credentials.

mitigations.name: Fitness App Privacy Settings
mitigations.description: Disable public profiles, activity sharing, and social features on fitness platforms.

mitigations.name: Wearable Device Reset
mitigations.description: Factory reset wearable devices and configure with sole-controlled account.

detections.name: Health Data Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary references exercise patterns, sleep data, health metrics, or location data from fitness tracking.

detections.name: Active Health Data Sharing
detections.description: Audit reveals fitness or health apps sharing data with adversary's account.

detections.name: Wearable Account Linkage
detections.description: Fitness tracker connected to adversary-controlled account.

techniques.name: Credential Theft
techniques.description: Obtaining victim's passwords, PINs, or authentication credentials through shoulder surfing, guessing based on personal knowledge, social engineering, checking common password patterns, or accessing written password records. Intimate partners often have enough personal knowledge to guess passwords or know where credentials are stored.
techniques.public_summary: Someone gets hold of your passwords — by watching you type them, guessing them, finding them written down, or using tools that capture what you type.
techniques.safety_warning: If you suspect someone has your passwords, changing them may alert them. Plan which accounts to secure first and change them from a safe device.

notices.signal: Account settings have changed without your input
notices.detail: Profile information, recovery emails, or security questions have been altered.

notices.signal: You receive password reset notifications you didn't request
notices.detail: Someone may be attempting to access or test your accounts.

notices.signal: The other person logs into your accounts or references private account content
notices.detail: They mention emails, messages, or information only accessible through your accounts.

actions.action: Change passwords from a device the other person hasn't accessed
actions.detail: Use a trusted friend's device or a library computer.
actions.safety_note: Don't change passwords on a device that might have monitoring software.

actions.action: Use unique, strong passwords for every account
actions.detail: A password manager can help you create and remember complex passwords.

actions.action: Enable two-factor authentication
actions.detail: This adds a second step (like a code sent to your phone) when logging in.
actions.safety_note: Make sure the second factor goes to a device only you control.

mitigations.name: Password Manager Deployment
mitigations.description: Use password manager with strong master password. Generate unique passwords for all accounts.

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.description: Enable MFA on all accounts using authenticator app on secure device.

mitigations.name: Credential Entry Security
mitigations.description: Use privacy screens. Avoid password entry where adversary can observe.

mitigations.name: Post-Separation Credential Reset
mitigations.description: Change all passwords after separation, starting with email accounts.

detections.name: Unauthorised Access Alerts
detections.description: Login notifications from unrecognised devices or locations.

detections.name: Account Lockout Events
detections.description: Unable to access accounts with previously valid credentials.

detections.name: Account Content Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary demonstrates knowledge of account-specific content.

sub_techniques.name: Coerced Biometric Access
sub_techniques.description: Forcing or tricking the victim into unlocking devices with fingerprint or face recognition while asleep, intoxicated, or under duress. May include physically placing the victim's finger on the sensor while they sleep. Bypasses all password security and leaves no digital trace — the unlock looks legitimate to the device.
sub_techniques.public_title: Someone unlocking your phone with your face or fingerprint while you're asleep
sub_techniques.public_summary: If someone holds your phone to your face or places your finger on the sensor while you're asleep or incapacitated, they can access everything on your device. It leaves no trace — the phone just sees a normal unlock.

notices.signal: Your phone shows it was used at times you were asleep
notices.detail: Check screen time or battery usage for activity during hours you were definitely asleep.

notices.signal: Someone knows content from your phone they shouldn't
notices.detail: Messages read, photos seen, apps checked — while you were sleeping.

actions.action: Switch from biometric to PIN/password
actions.detail: A PIN can't be used while you're asleep. A face or fingerprint can. For at-risk situations, PIN is more secure.

actions.action: Enable lockdown mode before sleeping
actions.detail: Both iOS and Android have lockdown/power-off options that disable biometric unlock. Use this overnight.

techniques.name: Account Takeover
techniques.description: Gaining full control of victim's accounts including email, social media, banking, government services, or utilities by changing credentials and recovery options. Complete takeover denies victim access while giving perpetrator full control over the account, including stored data, communications, and financial functions.
techniques.public_summary: Someone gains full control of one or more of your accounts — changing the password and recovery options so you can no longer access them.
techniques.safety_warning: Account takeover can be used to impersonate you. If you've lost access to an account, contact the platform's support immediately.

notices.signal: You're suddenly locked out of an account
notices.detail: Your password no longer works and recovery options have been changed.

notices.signal: Friends receive messages from your account that you didn't send
notices.detail: The other person may be using your account to impersonate you.

notices.signal: Your account profile or information has been changed
notices.detail: Name, photo, bio, or linked accounts have been altered.

actions.action: Contact the platform's account recovery support immediately
actions.detail: Most major platforms have processes for recovering hijacked accounts. Act quickly.

actions.action: Notify your contacts
actions.detail: Let people know your account has been compromised so they don't trust messages coming from it.

actions.action: Document everything
actions.detail: Screenshot any changes, messages sent from your account, and your attempts to recover it.

actions.action: Report to the platform and to police
actions.detail: Account takeover is a criminal offence. File reports with both.

mitigations.name: Account Documentation
mitigations.description: Document all account details including usernames, associated contacts, and creation dates for recovery purposes.

mitigations.name: Recovery Contact Security
mitigations.description: Change recovery email and phone to adversary-unknown contacts.

mitigations.name: Platform Recovery Engagement
mitigations.description: Contact platform support for account recovery. Many platforms have DFV-specific recovery processes.

detections.name: Complete Account Lockout
detections.description: Unable to access accounts. Password reset attempts fail or redirect to unknown contacts.

detections.name: Unauthorised Profile Changes
detections.description: Contacts report changes to profile content not made by account owner.

detections.name: Recovery Option Modification
detections.description: Account recovery reveals changed backup contacts or security questions.

techniques.name: Password/Recovery Change
techniques.description: Changing passwords and recovery options (backup email, phone number, security questions) on victim's accounts to lock them out and prevent recovery. This technique ensures persistent denial of access even if victim attempts account recovery procedures.
techniques.public_summary: Someone changes the recovery email, phone number, or security questions on your accounts — so that if you try to reset your password, the reset goes to them instead of you.

notices.signal: You can't recover your account using your usual method
notices.detail: Your recovery email or phone number has been changed.

notices.signal: You receive notifications about recovery option changes you didn't make
notices.detail: Platforms often send alerts when recovery details are updated.

notices.signal: Security questions or backup codes have been modified
notices.detail: Answers to your security questions no longer work.

actions.action: Set up recovery options the other person can't access
actions.detail: Use a new email address or phone number they don't know about.

actions.action: Enable login notifications
actions.detail: Get alerted every time someone logs into your account from a new device.

actions.action: Regularly check your account recovery settings
actions.detail: Make it a habit to verify your recovery email and phone number haven't changed.

mitigations.name: Multiple Recovery Methods
mitigations.description: Configure multiple recovery options so compromise of one does not eliminate account access.

mitigations.name: Security Question Hardening
mitigations.description: Use fictitious answers to security questions that adversary cannot guess from personal knowledge.

mitigations.name: Recovery Email Security
mitigations.description: Secure recovery email account with strong unique credentials and MFA.

detections.name: Unrequested Password Change Notifications
detections.description: Receiving confirmation of password or security changes not initiated by account owner.

detections.name: Recovery Method Change Alerts
detections.description: Notifications of backup email, phone, or security question changes.

techniques.name: Session Hijacking
techniques.description: Maintaining persistent access to victim's logged-in sessions by keeping devices logged in, copying session tokens, or exploiting 'remember this device' features. Allows perpetrator to monitor accounts without triggering new login alerts, making detection more difficult.
techniques.public_summary: Someone accesses your accounts by using a session that's already logged in — such as a browser you forgot to sign out of on a shared device, or by copying your login session data.

notices.signal: Your account shows active sessions on devices you don't recognise
notices.detail: Check the 'active sessions' or 'logged-in devices' section of your accounts.

notices.signal: Someone is reading new messages in real-time
notices.detail: Messages are marked as read before you open them, or the other person responds to things instantly.

notices.signal: Account activity at times when you weren't online
notices.detail: Login timestamps or activity logs show use when you were asleep or away.

actions.action: Sign out of all sessions on important accounts
actions.detail: Most platforms have a 'Sign out everywhere' option in security settings.

actions.action: Never save passwords on shared or public devices
actions.detail: Always use private/incognito mode on shared computers and sign out when done.

actions.action: Check your active sessions regularly
actions.detail: Review logged-in devices weekly on your key accounts.

mitigations.name: Active Session Monitoring
mitigations.description: Regularly review active sessions on all accounts. Terminate unrecognised sessions.

mitigations.name: Session Termination
mitigations.description: Use 'sign out all sessions' feature after credential changes.

detections.name: Unknown Active Sessions
detections.description: Session review shows sign-ins from unrecognised devices or locations.

detections.name: Unauthorised Account Activity
detections.description: Settings changed or content accessed without user action. Review platform activity logs.

techniques.name: Device Lockout
techniques.description: Remotely locking victim's phone, tablet, or computer through device management features such as Find My iPhone, Google Find My Device, or enterprise MDM tools. Can render devices completely unusable, cutting victim off from communication, navigation, banking, and emergency services.
techniques.public_title: Locking You Out of Your Devices
techniques.public_summary: Someone locks you out of your own phone, tablet, or computer — by changing the passcode, using remote lock features, or triggering factory resets.
techniques.safety_warning: Being locked out of your phone can be a safety risk in an emergency. Consider having a backup way to contact emergency services.

notices.signal: Your device passcode suddenly stops working
notices.detail: The password, PIN, or biometric you set has been changed.

notices.signal: Your device has been remotely wiped or reset
notices.detail: All your data, photos, and apps are gone.

notices.signal: You receive a message saying your device is locked
notices.detail: Features like 'Find My iPhone' or 'Find My Device' can be used to remotely lock a device.

actions.action: Contact your device manufacturer's support
actions.detail: Apple, Samsung, and Google all have processes for recovering locked devices.

actions.action: Use a different device to secure your cloud accounts
actions.detail: If your phone is locked, secure your iCloud, Google, or Microsoft accounts from another device immediately.

actions.action: Keep your cloud account credentials separate and private
actions.detail: The person who controls your iCloud or Google account can remotely control your device.

mitigations.name: Remote Management Removal
mitigations.description: Remove device from adversary's Find My/Find My Device account.

mitigations.name: Account Migration
mitigations.description: Migrate device to sole-controlled Apple ID or Google account. Factory reset if required.

detections.name: Remote Lock Activation
detections.description: Device displays lock screen or lost mode message without user action.

detections.name: Remote Wipe Execution
detections.description: Device factory resets without user initiation.

techniques.name: Two-Factor Interception
techniques.description: Intercepting two-factor authentication codes through SIM swapping, access to victim's authenticator app, interception of SMS codes, or control of backup codes. Defeats security measures designed to protect accounts, enabling unauthorized access even when victim has changed passwords.
techniques.public_summary: Someone intercepts the security codes sent to verify your identity — by accessing your text messages, SIM-swapping your phone number, or using a device you've already trusted.

notices.signal: You stop receiving text messages or calls
notices.detail: Your SIM may have been swapped — the other person has transferred your number to their device.

notices.signal: Login codes arrive on a device you don't control
notices.detail: Security codes are going to a phone or email the other person has access to.

notices.signal: Your mobile service suddenly stops working
notices.detail: SIM swap attacks cause your phone to lose signal entirely.

actions.action: Switch to an authenticator app instead of SMS codes
actions.detail: Apps like Google Authenticator or Authy generate codes on your device, which is harder to intercept than text messages.

actions.action: Set a PIN or password on your mobile account
actions.detail: Contact your carrier and add a security PIN to prevent SIM swaps.

actions.action: Use a phone number the other person doesn't know
actions.detail: A separate prepaid number for two-factor authentication adds a layer of protection.

mitigations.name: Authenticator App Security
mitigations.description: Use authenticator app on secure device rather than SMS-based 2FA.

mitigations.name: SIM Security Controls
mitigations.description: Contact carrier to add SIM lock PIN and port-out protection.

mitigations.name: Hardware Security Key
mitigations.description: Use hardware security key for highest-risk accounts.

detections.name: SIM Swap Indicators
detections.description: Sudden loss of mobile service may indicate SIM swap attack.

detections.name: Unrequested 2FA Codes
detections.description: Receiving 2FA codes without initiating login attempts.

techniques.name: Backup/Cloud Access
techniques.description: Accessing victim's personal data through cloud backup services such as iCloud, Google Drive, OneDrive, or device backups. Cloud backups often contain comprehensive copies of messages, photos, contacts, browsing history, and app data, providing extensive surveillance capability from a single access point.
techniques.public_summary: Someone accesses your cloud storage or device backups — seeing your photos, documents, messages, and other data stored in services like iCloud, Google Drive, or Dropbox.
techniques.safety_warning: Cloud backups can contain a complete copy of your digital life. Securing your cloud accounts is critical.

notices.signal: The other person has seen photos or documents you only stored in the cloud
notices.detail: They reference files you haven't shared with anyone.

notices.signal: Storage notifications about activity you didn't do
notices.detail: Files accessed, downloaded, or deleted without your knowledge.

notices.signal: Unfamiliar devices connected to your cloud account
notices.detail: Check which devices are linked to your iCloud, Google, or Microsoft account.

actions.action: Review which devices are connected to your cloud accounts
actions.detail: iCloud: Settings > Apple ID > Devices. Google: myaccount.google.com > Security > Your devices.

actions.action: Change your cloud account password from a safe device
actions.detail: This is often the single most important step.
actions.safety_note: A cloud account password often controls everything — email, photos, backups, location.

actions.action: Remove unknown devices and revoke their access
actions.detail: Sign out any device you don't recognise.

mitigations.name: Cloud Account Security
mitigations.description: Change passwords and enable MFA on cloud storage. Review and remove sharing permissions.

mitigations.name: Backup Encryption
mitigations.description: Enable encrypted backups where available.

detections.name: Cloud Access Alerts
detections.description: Sign-in alerts for cloud services from unfamiliar devices or locations.

detections.name: Cloud Content Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary demonstrates knowledge of cloud-only content.

techniques.name: Shared Account Weaponization
techniques.description: Using legitimately shared accounts for streaming services, utilities, subscriptions, or household management to exert control or punish victim. Includes changing shared passwords, cancelling shared services, monitoring usage patterns, or using account features to track victim's activity and preferences.
techniques.public_summary: Someone weaponizes accounts you set up together — deleting shared photos, changing subscription settings, removing your access, or using shared content against you.

notices.signal: Shared content starts disappearing
notices.detail: Photos, documents, or files from shared accounts are being deleted.

notices.signal: You lose access to subscriptions or services
notices.detail: Shared streaming, utility, or service accounts are modified or cancelled.

notices.signal: Shared account content is used to embarrass or control you
notices.detail: Private content from shared accounts is shared with others or used as leverage.

actions.action: Back up any important shared content to your own account
actions.detail: Copy photos, documents, and files you need before separating accounts.

actions.action: Create your own individual accounts for essential services
actions.detail: Set up fresh accounts for streaming, utilities, and other services.

actions.action: Document what exists in shared accounts
actions.detail: Screenshot or save records of shared content in case it's deleted.

mitigations.name: Shared Account Separation
mitigations.description: Systematically separate shared accounts for streaming, utilities, and subscriptions.

mitigations.name: Shared Account Documentation
mitigations.description: Document all shared account details before separation.

detections.name: Shared Service Disruption
detections.description: Shared services cancelled, passwords changed, or access revoked without discussion.

detections.name: Weaponized Account Activity
detections.description: Adversary uses shared account access to monitor activity or make changes as control mechanism.

techniques.name: Device Sabotage
techniques.description: Deliberately damaging, corrupting, factory-resetting, or wiping victim's devices or data. May involve physical damage, remote wipe commands, malware installation, or deliberate corruption of important files. Destroys evidence, disrupts victim's ability to communicate, and causes emotional and financial harm.
techniques.public_summary: Someone deliberately damages, misconfigures, or interferes with your phone, computer, or other devices to make them unreliable, slow, or unusable.
techniques.safety_warning: Device sabotage can be a precursor to escalation. If your devices are being interfered with, tell someone you trust.

notices.signal: Your devices keep malfunctioning in ways you can't explain
notices.detail: Settings change, apps crash, or the device behaves erratically.

notices.signal: Problems only happen after the other person has had access
notices.detail: The device works fine, then has issues after they've been near it.

notices.signal: Factory resets or data wipes you didn't authorise
notices.detail: Your device has been wiped, losing your contacts, photos, and messages.

actions.action: Keep your device physically secure
actions.detail: Don't leave it unattended when the other person could access it.

actions.action: Back up your data regularly to a secure location
actions.detail: Use cloud backup with an account only you control.

actions.action: Document the pattern
actions.detail: Keep a log of device issues with dates and whether the other person had access.

mitigations.name: Data Backup Protocol
mitigations.description: Maintain regular backups to adversary-inaccessible storage.

mitigations.name: Physical Device Security
mitigations.description: Maintain physical control of devices. Store evidence in secure cloud storage.

detections.name: Unexplained Data Loss
detections.description: Files, photos, or messages disappearing without user action.

detections.name: Device Damage or Reset
detections.description: Devices physically damaged or factory reset during adversary access periods.

techniques.name: Administrative Access Abuse
techniques.description: Using parental controls, family administrator privileges, or enterprise MDM capabilities to exert control over an adult victim's devices and accounts. Exploits legitimate administrative tools designed for child safety or corporate security to restrict an adult's digital autonomy.
techniques.public_summary: Someone who has administrative control over shared devices, networks, or accounts uses that access to monitor, restrict, or control you.
techniques.safety_warning: Admin access can give someone total control over your digital environment. If you suspect this, seek specialist tech safety help.

notices.signal: Your permissions keep getting changed
notices.detail: You lose access to features, apps, or settings that used to work.

notices.signal: Content or downloads are being blocked
notices.detail: Websites, apps, or content you try to access are restricted.

notices.signal: The other person can see or change things on your device remotely
notices.detail: Settings, wallpapers, or configurations change without your input.

actions.action: Identify who has admin access to your devices and accounts
actions.detail: Check device management profiles, admin accounts on shared computers, and router access.

actions.action: Get your own separate devices and accounts
actions.detail: A device you set up yourself, on your own account, that the other person never touches.

actions.action: Remove mobile device management (MDM) profiles
actions.detail: On iPhone: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management. Remove profiles you didn't install.
actions.safety_note: This may alert the admin.

mitigations.name: Administrative Control Removal
mitigations.description: Remove parental control software and MDM profiles. Factory reset if removal not possible.

mitigations.name: Family Group Exit
mitigations.description: Leave family sharing groups that grant adversary administrative control.

detections.name: Unexpected Device Restrictions
detections.description: Apps blocked, websites inaccessible, or features limited by parental controls not installed by user.

detections.name: Usage Reports to Adversary
detections.description: Screen Time or similar tools sending activity reports to adversary's account.

techniques.name: Direct Threat Messaging
techniques.description: Sending threatening messages to victim via any digital platform, including text messages, emails, direct messages, voice messages, or comments. Threats may be explicit (threatening violence, harm, or consequences) or implicit (veiled references to harm, ominous statements, or threatening imagery).
techniques.public_summary: Someone sends you threatening messages through any digital platform — texts, emails, social media, or messaging apps. Threats may be explicit or veiled.
techniques.safety_warning: If you feel you're in immediate danger, contact 000. Save all threatening messages as evidence.

notices.signal: You receive messages that threaten violence or harm
notices.detail: Direct or implied threats to you, your children, your pets, or your property.

notices.signal: Threatening images or media are sent to you
notices.detail: Photos of weapons, your home, or other intimidating content.

notices.signal: Threats are disguised as concern or 'warnings'
notices.detail: Messages framed as 'I'm worried what might happen if...' or 'It would be a shame if...'

actions.action: Screenshot and save every threatening message
actions.detail: Include the sender's details, timestamps, and the platform. Save to a secure location.

actions.action: Don't respond to threats
actions.detail: Responding can escalate the situation and encourage further contact.

actions.action: Report to both the platform and police
actions.detail: Most platforms have specific reporting for threats. File a police report as well.

actions.action: Consider an Apprehended Violence Order (AVO)
actions.detail: Courts can order the person to stop contacting you. A lawyer or support service can help.

mitigations.name: Evidence Preservation
mitigations.description: Screenshot and save all threatening messages with timestamps and sender details.

mitigations.name: Platform and Law Enforcement Reporting
mitigations.description: Report threats to platform and police. Preserve evidence for legal proceedings.

mitigations.name: Communication Boundary Enforcement
mitigations.description: Establish communication boundaries. Block on platforms where no legitimate contact required.

detections.name: Threatening Content Receipt
detections.description: Messages containing explicit or implicit threats of harm or adverse consequences.

detections.name: Escalation Pattern
detections.description: Message tone becoming increasingly aggressive or menacing over time.

sub_techniques.name: Coded Threat Language
sub_techniques.description: Threats disguised as benign messages that only the victim understands the meaning of. 'I drove past your favourite park today.' 'Saw someone who looked like you at the shops.' Looks innocent to police, courts, and anyone else — but the victim knows exactly what it means. The shared history between perpetrator and victim is the cipher.
sub_techniques.public_title: Messages that sound innocent but you know are threats
sub_techniques.public_summary: They send messages that would look harmless to anyone else — but you know what they really mean. 'I was in your area today.' 'I thought about you when I saw [something specific].' The threat is real but invisible to everyone except you.

notices.signal: Messages that reference places, people, or events with hidden meaning
notices.detail: They mention your workplace, your child's school, or a specific location — and you know it's a threat, not a casual comment.

notices.signal: You feel afraid but can't explain why to anyone reading the message
notices.detail: The words look innocent on paper. The fear you feel is based on context only you have.

actions.action: Keep a log that explains the context
actions.detail: Write down what each message means to you and why. 'When they say X, they mean Y because of Z incident.' This context is evidence.

actions.action: Tell a DV specialist about the pattern
actions.detail: Family violence services understand coded threats. They can help you document and explain the pattern to police and courts.

techniques.name: Persistent Unwanted Contact
techniques.description: Repeatedly contacting victim despite clear requests to stop, across one or multiple communication platforms. Volume and persistence are used to exhaust, intimidate, and demonstrate that the victim cannot escape the perpetrator's reach. May include hundreds of messages, calls, or contact attempts per day.
techniques.public_summary: Someone bombards you with constant messages, calls, voicemails, or contact attempts — dozens or hundreds a day — to overwhelm, exhaust, or frighten you.

notices.signal: Overwhelming volume of messages, calls, or notifications
notices.detail: Dozens or hundreds of messages across multiple platforms.

notices.signal: Contact continues despite you asking them to stop
notices.detail: Clear requests to stop are ignored.

notices.signal: The content cycles between hostile, loving, and desperate
notices.detail: The tone swings wildly — threats, then apologies, then anger again.

actions.action: Block across all platforms but save evidence first
actions.detail: Screenshot the volume of messages before blocking. You may need this for legal proceedings.

actions.action: Enable 'Do Not Disturb' or silence unknown callers
actions.detail: Reduce the immediate impact while preserving evidence in the background.

actions.action: Document the pattern
actions.detail: Keep a log of dates, times, number of contacts, and platforms used.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Persistent unwanted contact can constitute stalking. File a report.

mitigations.name: Contact Documentation
mitigations.description: Maintain log of all unwanted contact with dates, times, platforms, and content.

mitigations.name: Block and Filter Strategy
mitigations.description: Block adversary on all platforms. Configure email filters to archive messages for evidence.

mitigations.name: Carrier Harassment Report
mitigations.description: Contact phone carrier to report harassment and implement call blocking.

detections.name: High Volume Contact
detections.description: Unreasonable number of contact attempts across channels.

detections.name: Multi-Platform Contact Pattern
detections.description: Simultaneous contact attempts across multiple platforms.

techniques.name: Contact After Blocking
techniques.description: Creating new accounts, using alternative platforms, borrowing others' devices, or finding other channels to continue contacting victim after being blocked. Demonstrates persistent intent to circumvent victim's boundaries and platform safety features.
techniques.public_summary: After being blocked, someone finds ways to keep contacting you — using new accounts, new phone numbers, other people's devices, or different platforms.

notices.signal: New unknown accounts contact you with familiar language
notices.detail: The writing style, pet names, or references make it clear who it is.

notices.signal: Messages arrive from unknown numbers saying things only the person would know
notices.detail: They create new accounts or get new numbers specifically to reach you.

notices.signal: Contact comes through unexpected platforms
notices.detail: They find you on platforms you thought they didn't know about.

actions.action: Keep blocking new accounts but document each one
actions.detail: Each new attempt to circumvent blocking is evidence of a pattern.

actions.action: Adjust privacy settings so only approved contacts can message you
actions.detail: Many platforms allow you to restrict messages to friends/followers only.

actions.action: Report the pattern to police
actions.detail: Circumventing blocking to maintain unwanted contact strengthens a stalking case.

mitigations.name: Multi-Platform Block Maintenance
mitigations.description: Maintain blocks across platforms. Enable unknown sender filtering.

mitigations.name: Ban Evasion Reporting
mitigations.description: Report new accounts to platforms for ban evasion.

detections.name: New Accounts with Adversary Indicators
detections.description: New accounts using familiar language patterns or referencing personal details.

detections.name: Alternative Channel Contact
detections.description: Contact via channels not previously used after blocking on primary platforms.

techniques.name: Coordinated Harassment Campaign
techniques.description: Organizing or inciting multiple people to simultaneously harass victim through pile-ons, brigading, coordinated reporting, mass messaging, or targeted online mob behavior. Perpetrator may directly recruit participants or create conditions that provoke organic harassment from communities.
techniques.public_summary: Someone coordinates others to harass you — directing friends, followers, or online communities to send you abusive messages, leave negative reviews, or attack you online.
techniques.safety_warning: Coordinated harassment can feel overwhelming. You don't have to deal with it alone — support services can help.

notices.signal: Sudden wave of hostile messages from people you don't know
notices.detail: Multiple strangers contact you with similar themes or language.

notices.signal: Abusive reviews or comments appear across your online presence
notices.detail: Your business, social media, or public profiles are targeted simultaneously.

notices.signal: The abuse follows a recognisable pattern or narrative
notices.detail: The attackers seem to be working from the same story about you.

actions.action: Don't engage with individual attackers
actions.detail: Responding fuels the campaign. Focus on documentation and reporting.

actions.action: Report the coordination to platforms
actions.detail: Most platforms prohibit coordinated harassment. Report the pattern, not just individual messages.

actions.action: Lock down your online presence temporarily
actions.detail: Set accounts to private, disable comments, and restrict who can message you.

actions.action: Preserve evidence of coordination
actions.detail: Screenshot posts directing others to attack you.

mitigations.name: Mass Block and Report
mitigations.description: Block and report all participating accounts. Report coordinated harassment pattern to platform.

mitigations.name: Temporary Account Restriction
mitigations.description: Temporarily restrict account access and disable comments during active campaign.

mitigations.name: Regulatory Body Report
mitigations.description: Report serious coordinated harassment to eSafety Commissioner or equivalent body.

detections.name: Hostile Interaction Spike
detections.description: Rapid increase in negative interactions from multiple accounts.

detections.name: Coordination Indicators
detections.description: Multiple accounts using similar language, talking points, or hashtags.

techniques.name: Doxxing
techniques.description: Publishing victim's private information (home address, phone number, workplace, family members, daily routines) publicly or to targeted audiences with intent to enable harassment, stalking, or physical harm. Doxxing weaponizes personal information by removing the victim's control over who has access to it, often resulting in coordinated harassment, threats, and real-world danger.
techniques.public_summary: Someone publishes your private information online — your home address, phone number, workplace, children's school, or other personal details — to expose you or invite harassment.
techniques.safety_warning: If your address has been published and you feel unsafe, contact police. Consider temporary accommodation if there's an immediate threat.

notices.signal: Strangers reference your personal details
notices.detail: People you don't know mention your address, workplace, or other private information.

notices.signal: You find your personal information posted on public websites or forums
notices.detail: Your details have been shared without your consent.

notices.signal: You receive unwanted contact at locations only known through doxxing
notices.detail: People show up at your home or workplace.

actions.action: Report to the platform where your information was published
actions.detail: Request urgent removal of your personal details.

actions.action: Contact the eSafety Commissioner
