actions.detail: In Australia, the eSafety Commissioner can help with the removal of doxxed information.

actions.action: Alert your workplace, school, and building security
actions.detail: Let relevant people know your information has been compromised.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Doxxing can constitute stalking or intimidation.

mitigations.name: Personal Information Minimisation
mitigations.description: Audit and remove personal information from public sources. Opt out of data broker sites.

mitigations.name: Address and Contact Protection
mitigations.description: Use PO Box for mail. Register domains with privacy protection.

mitigations.name: Doxxing Response Protocol
mitigations.description: If doxxed: report to police, request content removal, alert workplace, document everything.

detections.name: Personal Information Published
detections.description: Private information appears on public platforms.

detections.name: Stranger Harassment Based on Published Details
detections.description: Contact from unknown individuals referencing doxxed information.

techniques.name: Swatting
techniques.description: Making false emergency reports (bomb threats, hostage situations, active shooter calls) to provoke armed law enforcement response at victim's location. Swatting creates immediate physical danger to victim and household, causes severe psychological trauma, and may result in injury or death from police response.
techniques.public_title: False Emergency Calls to Your Address
techniques.public_summary: Someone makes false emergency calls to send police, ambulances, or fire services to your address — creating a frightening and potentially dangerous situation.
techniques.safety_warning: Swatting can be life-threatening. If you believe you're at risk of swatting, inform your local police station proactively.

notices.signal: Emergency services arrive at your home without you calling them
notices.detail: Police, paramedics, or fire services respond to calls you didn't make.

notices.signal: You learn that false reports have been filed about you
notices.detail: Reports to police, child protection, or other services that are fabricated.

actions.action: Proactively brief your local police station
actions.detail: Explain the risk and ask for your address to be flagged.

actions.action: Report false calls as a criminal offence
actions.detail: Making false emergency calls is illegal. Gather evidence the calls are fabricated.

actions.action: Keep documentation of all false reports
actions.detail: Create a chronological record with dates and responding agencies.

mitigations.name: Law Enforcement Notification
mitigations.description: Notify local police of false report risk. Request address flagging in dispatch system.

mitigations.name: Emergency Response Preparation
mitigations.description: Prepare for calm interaction with emergency services. Brief household members.

detections.name: Unexpected Emergency Response
detections.description: Emergency services arrive in response to unrequested call.

detections.name: False Report Pattern
detections.description: Multiple false reports correlating with relationship events.

techniques.name: Platform Abuse Reporting
techniques.description: Weaponizing platform content moderation and reporting systems to get victim's accounts banned, restricted, or content removed. Perpetrator files false or exaggerated reports about victim's content, coordinating multiple reports to trigger automated enforcement. Silences victim and removes their online presence.
techniques.public_summary: Someone files false reports against your accounts — trying to get your social media, business pages, or content removed by abusing platform reporting systems.

notices.signal: Your content or accounts are removed for violations you didn't commit
notices.detail: Posts, pages, or accounts are taken down after false reports.

notices.signal: You receive repeated warnings from platforms
notices.detail: Multiple reports trigger automated warnings or restrictions.

notices.signal: Your business or professional presence is affected
notices.detail: Reviews, listings, or professional profiles are disrupted.

actions.action: Appeal every false takedown
actions.detail: Platforms have appeal processes. Use them consistently and document each one.

actions.action: Document the pattern of false reports
actions.detail: Keep records of each takedown with dates and details.

actions.action: Contact platform support directly
actions.detail: Explain the pattern of abuse and request account protection.

mitigations.name: Content Backup
mitigations.description: Regularly backup social media content using platform export tools.

mitigations.name: Appeal Process Utilisation
mitigations.description: Appeal account restrictions with context about weaponised reporting pattern.

detections.name: Unjustified Account Restrictions
detections.description: Content removed or account restricted for non-violating posts during conflict periods.

detections.name: Multiple Report Indicators
detections.description: Platform communications indicating multiple reports against account.

techniques.name: Public Humiliation Posts
techniques.description: Posting embarrassing, mocking, degrading, or humiliating content about victim on public platforms. Content may include unflattering images, private information, personal struggles, or fabricated scenarios designed to damage victim's social standing and cause emotional harm.
techniques.public_summary: Someone posts content designed to publicly humiliate, embarrass, or shame you — sharing private information, embarrassing images, or fabricated stories about you.

notices.signal: People you know reference embarrassing content about you online
notices.detail: Friends, colleagues, or acquaintances have seen posts about you.

notices.signal: Humiliating content appears on the other person's or their friends' social media
notices.detail: Posts that mock, shame, or expose private matters.

notices.signal: Your private information or images are shared in group chats or forums
notices.detail: Content circulates beyond the original post.

actions.action: Report content to the platform for removal
actions.detail: Most platforms remove content designed to harass or bully.

actions.action: Contact the eSafety Commissioner if content includes intimate images
actions.detail: In Australia, non-consensual intimate image sharing can be actioned through eSafety.

actions.action: Avoid responding publicly
actions.detail: Public responses can fuel further sharing. Focus on removal and reporting.

actions.action: Save evidence before it's deleted
actions.detail: The poster may delete content later — screenshot everything first.

mitigations.name: Content Removal Request
mitigations.description: Report humiliating content to platform. Report to regulatory body for serious content.

mitigations.name: Search Result Management
mitigations.description: Request deindexing of harmful content. Create positive content to influence search results.

detections.name: Harmful Content Discovery
detections.description: Posts containing embarrassing or private content about target.

detections.name: Third-Party Content Alerts
detections.description: Contacts report encountering harmful content online.

techniques.name: Impersonation Harassment
techniques.description: Creating fake accounts impersonating victim to damage their reputation, relationships, or employment. Fake accounts may send messages to victim's contacts, post inappropriate content, engage in harmful activities, or create the appearance that victim is behaving erratically or antisocially.
techniques.public_summary: Someone creates fake accounts impersonating you — using your name, photos, and personal details to damage your reputation, harass others in your name, or create confusion.

notices.signal: People tell you about accounts or messages 'from you' that you didn't create or send
notices.detail: Friends receive messages from someone pretending to be you.

notices.signal: Fake profiles using your photos and name appear on social media or dating sites
notices.detail: Your identity is being used without your consent.

notices.signal: You're blamed for things the impersonator said or did
notices.detail: People are angry at you for things you didn't do.

actions.action: Report impersonation accounts to the platform immediately
actions.detail: All major platforms have dedicated impersonation reporting tools.

actions.action: Notify your contacts
actions.detail: Let people know about the fake accounts so they're not deceived.

actions.action: Document the fake accounts
actions.detail: Screenshot profiles, messages, and any damage caused.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Impersonation for the purpose of harassment is a criminal offence.

mitigations.name: Impersonation Reporting
mitigations.description: Report fake accounts to platform using impersonation reporting process.

mitigations.name: Network Notification
mitigations.description: Inform contacts of fake accounts and request verification through trusted channels.

detections.name: Contact Reports of Impersonation Messages
detections.description: Contacts report receiving messages from accounts impersonating target.

detections.name: Fake Account Discovery
detections.description: Profiles using target's name, photos, or information discovered.

techniques.name: Review/Rating Attacks
techniques.description: Posting false negative reviews of victim's business, professional profiles, or services across review platforms. Damages victim's professional reputation, income, and career prospects. May coordinate multiple fake reviews to appear credible.
techniques.public_summary: Someone posts fake negative reviews about your business, professional services, or public presence — using fabricated or exaggerated claims to damage your livelihood.

notices.signal: A sudden cluster of negative reviews from accounts with no history
notices.detail: Reviews appear from profiles that were recently created or have no other activity.

notices.signal: Reviews contain personal attacks rather than genuine customer feedback
notices.detail: The content is about you personally, not about a product or service.

notices.signal: The timing correlates with conflict with the other person
notices.detail: Bad reviews appear after arguments, separation, or legal action.

actions.action: Report fake reviews to the platform
actions.detail: Google, Facebook, and other review platforms have processes for flagging fake reviews.

actions.action: Respond professionally to reviews you can't get removed
actions.detail: A calm, factual response shows other readers the reviews aren't genuine.

actions.action: Document the connection between reviews and the other person
actions.detail: Pattern evidence strengthens any legal or platform complaint.

mitigations.name: False Review Dispute
mitigations.description: Flag false reviews for removal. Provide evidence of fraudulent origin.

mitigations.name: Review Response Strategy
mitigations.description: Respond professionally to false reviews. Request genuine client reviews to counterbalance.

detections.name: Fraudulent Review Pattern
detections.description: Negative reviews from non-genuine accounts correlating with conflict events.

detections.name: Professional Impact
detections.description: Decline in business correlating with review attack.

techniques.name: Contact Bombing
techniques.description: Signing victim up for large volumes of spam, unwanted subscriptions, mailing lists, or services to overwhelm their communications and cause distress. May also include signing victim up for politically sensitive, embarrassing, or compromising services.
techniques.public_title: Signing You Up for Unwanted Services
techniques.public_summary: Someone signs your phone number or email up for hundreds of services, newsletters, or verification codes — flooding you with constant notifications and messages.

notices.signal: Sudden flood of verification codes, newsletters, or spam
notices.detail: Your phone or email is overwhelmed with messages you didn't sign up for.

notices.signal: The volume makes it hard to find real, important messages
notices.detail: Legitimate messages from friends, work, or services are buried.

actions.action: Use email filtering rules to manage the flood
actions.detail: Set up filters to automatically sort or delete the spam.

actions.action: Report the pattern to your phone carrier
actions.detail: They may be able to help with SMS flooding.

actions.action: Consider a new phone number or email for important contacts
actions.detail: Share the new details only with trusted people.

mitigations.name: Email Filtering
mitigations.description: Configure email filtering to manage volume. Unsubscribe from spam subscriptions.

mitigations.name: Communication Channel Protection
mitigations.description: Consider temporary contact change while maintaining bombarded accounts for evidence.

detections.name: Spam Volume Spike
detections.description: Dramatic increase in spam, subscriptions, or marketing messages.

detections.name: Unrequested Sign-Up Confirmations
detections.description: Confirmation emails from services never subscribed to.

techniques.name: Proxy Harassment via AI
techniques.description: Using AI tools including large language models, voice cloning, or text generation to create and distribute harassing content at scale. AI enables perpetrators to generate personalized, varied harassment content more quickly and in greater volume than manual methods, and may disguise the perpetrator's authorship.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses AI tools to generate harassing content — fake images, fake audio of your voice, mass-produced abusive messages, or AI-written defamatory content about you.

notices.signal: Harassing content that seems AI-generated or mass-produced
notices.detail: Messages, images, or posts that feel formulaic or are produced in large volumes.

notices.signal: Fake images or audio that look or sound like you
notices.detail: AI-generated content using your likeness or voice.

notices.signal: Abusive content that's unusually varied or persistent
notices.detail: The volume and variety suggests automated generation.

actions.action: Report AI-generated harassment to platforms
actions.detail: Many platforms are developing specific policies for AI-generated abusive content.

actions.action: Preserve the content as evidence
actions.detail: AI-generated abuse is still abuse and can be reported to police.

actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner
actions.detail: AI-generated intimate images or targeted harassment falls within eSafety's remit.

mitigations.name: AI Content Detection
mitigations.description: Use AI detection tools to identify synthetic content for evidence purposes.

mitigations.name: Platform-Level Reporting
mitigations.description: Report automated abuse patterns to platforms rather than responding to individual items.

detections.name: Synthetic Language Patterns
detections.description: Messages that are formulaic, vary slightly while making same points, or arrive at unrealistic volumes.

detections.name: AI-Generated Media Indicators
detections.description: Media with artifacts characteristic of synthetic generation.

techniques.name: Message/Evidence Tampering
techniques.description: Editing, deleting, selectively screenshotting, or fabricating screenshots of conversations, messages, or digital records to misrepresent what was communicated. Used to create false evidence, destroy exculpatory evidence, or support false narratives in legal proceedings and social contexts.
techniques.public_summary: Someone edits, deletes, or fabricates digital messages and evidence — changing what was said in text conversations, deleting messages to change the narrative, or creating fake screenshots.
techniques.safety_warning: If you suspect evidence is being tampered with, start keeping your own independent records immediately.

notices.signal: Conversations look different from how you remember them
notices.detail: Messages appear edited, missing, or rearranged.

notices.signal: The other person shows 'evidence' of things you didn't say
notices.detail: Screenshots or messages that don't match your memory or records.

notices.signal: Messages in shared conversations have been selectively deleted
notices.detail: Key context is missing from threads.

actions.action: Keep your own copies of important conversations
actions.detail: Screenshot, export, or back up conversations regularly to a location only you control.

actions.action: Use platforms with edit history or deletion tracking
actions.detail: Some apps show when messages have been edited or deleted.

actions.action: Don't rely solely on digital records the other person can access
actions.detail: Keep physical notes or voice memos as backup records.

mitigations.name: Original Record Preservation
mitigations.description: Preserve original communications using platform export tools with metadata.

mitigations.name: Metadata Verification
mitigations.description: Use platform records with headers and metadata rather than screenshots for evidence.

mitigations.name: Witness Communication
mitigations.description: Include trusted witness in important communications for corroboration.

detections.name: Evidence Discrepancies
detections.description: Adversary-presented records don't match target's records of same communication.

detections.name: Message Alteration
detections.description: Messages deleted or content changed from what target recalls.

techniques.name: Digital Gaslighting
techniques.description: Manipulating digital records, device settings, files, or other digital artifacts to make victim doubt their own memory, perception, or sanity. Includes moving or deleting files, editing shared documents, changing device settings, manipulating photo timestamps, or altering digital records the victim relies on.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses technology to make you question your own memory and perception — deleting messages then denying they existed, changing settings then blaming you, or rewriting digital history.
techniques.safety_warning: If someone consistently makes you doubt your memory of digital interactions, that itself is a form of abuse. Trust your experience.

notices.signal: Things you remember seeing or reading online seem to have disappeared
notices.detail: Messages, posts, or settings you clearly remember are gone.

notices.signal: The other person insists events didn't happen the way you remember
notices.detail: They have a different version of a digital interaction you were part of.

notices.signal: Your device settings keep changing and you're told you must have done it yourself
notices.detail: Changes you didn't make are attributed to your own confusion.

actions.action: Start keeping a private journal of digital interactions
actions.detail: Write down what happened, when, in your own words. A handwritten journal can't be remotely altered.

actions.action: Screenshot important conversations immediately
actions.detail: Don't wait — capture the evidence before it can be changed or deleted.

actions.action: Trust your own experience
actions.detail: If your memory consistently differs from what the other person tells you, take that seriously.

mitigations.name: Digital State Documentation
mitigations.description: Screenshot settings and configurations to establish baseline. Log device states to detect changes.

mitigations.name: External Verification
mitigations.description: Verify noticed changes with trusted person before doubting own perception.

mitigations.name: Version History Monitoring
mitigations.description: Enable and check version history on shared documents to detect manipulation.

detections.name: Unexplained Setting Changes
detections.description: Device settings or file locations changed without user action. Check modification timestamps.

detections.name: Reality Questioning Pattern
detections.description: Increasing self-doubt about digital actions aligning with adversary's claims.

techniques.name: Non-Consensual Intimate Image Distribution
techniques.description: Sharing or threatening to share intimate, sexual, or nude images of victim without their consent. Commonly known as 'revenge porn,' this technique weaponizes intimate content to humiliate, control, or coerce victim. Includes sharing via private messages, posting publicly, uploading to pornographic websites, or sending to victim's contacts, family, or employer.
techniques.public_summary: Someone shares or threatens to share intimate, sexual, or nude images of you without your consent — sometimes called 'revenge porn'. This includes images that were taken consensually in a relationship but shared without permission.
techniques.safety_warning: This is a criminal offence in Australia. You can get help from the eSafety Commissioner and police. You are not to blame.

notices.signal: Someone tells you they've seen intimate images of you online
notices.detail: Images you thought were private have been shared.

notices.signal: The other person threatens to share images unless you comply with demands
notices.detail: Threats to distribute images are used as leverage.

notices.signal: Intimate images appear on websites, social media, or in group chats
notices.detail: Your images have been posted publicly or semi-publicly.

actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner immediately
actions.detail: eSafety has legal powers to compel platforms to remove intimate images quickly.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Non-consensual sharing of intimate images is a criminal offence in all Australian states.

actions.action: Don't try to get the images removed yourself by contacting each site
actions.detail: The eSafety Commissioner has more effective tools for this.

actions.action: Seek support
actions.detail: This can be deeply distressing. Services like 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) provide specialist support.

mitigations.name: Regulatory Body Report
mitigations.description: Report NCII to eSafety Commissioner or equivalent body with legal content removal powers.

mitigations.name: Hash-Based Prevention Registration
mitigations.description: Register images with StopNCII.org to prevent re-upload on participating platforms.

mitigations.name: Law Enforcement Report
mitigations.description: Report to police. NCII is criminal offence in most jurisdictions.

detections.name: Intimate Image Distribution Discovery
detections.description: Intimate images found on public platforms or reported by contacts.

detections.name: Distribution Threats
detections.description: Adversary threatens to share intimate images as leverage.

sub_techniques.name: AI-Enhanced NCII
sub_techniques.description: Taking non-intimate photos (social media photos, selfies, professional headshots) and using AI to generate nude or intimate versions. The victim never took or consented to an intimate image — the intimate image was fabricated from a clothed photo. Growing legal gap as some jurisdictions' laws require an 'original intimate image.'
sub_techniques.public_title: Someone has created fake intimate images of you using AI
sub_techniques.public_summary: Using artificial intelligence, someone has taken your ordinary photos — from social media, work, or everyday life — and generated fake nude or intimate images of you. You never took these photos. They were created without your knowledge or consent.

notices.signal: Intimate images of you appear that you never took
notices.detail: If intimate images exist that you didn't create and weren't taken of you, they may be AI-generated from your public photos.

notices.signal: The images look almost real but something is slightly off
notices.detail: AI-generated images may have subtle artefacts — unusual skin texture, inconsistent lighting, odd backgrounds.

actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner immediately
actions.detail: The eSafety Commissioner can issue removal notices to platforms hosting the images. esafety.gov.au

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Creating and distributing intimate images without consent is a criminal offence in Australia, regardless of whether the images are 'real.'

actions.action: Don't try to find or view the images yourself
actions.detail: Searching for them can be traumatising and may increase their visibility in search results.

techniques.name: Deepfake Creation
techniques.description: Creating synthetic intimate, compromising, or damaging media of victim using AI-powered deepfake technology. Generated content may be indistinguishable from real imagery and can be used for extortion, reputational harm, or psychological abuse. Includes face-swapping onto pornographic content, synthetic voice generation, or fabricated video.
techniques.public_title: Creating Fake Images or Videos of You
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses AI or editing tools to create realistic fake images or videos of you — often sexual content — using your face or likeness placed onto other bodies or in fabricated scenarios.
techniques.safety_warning: AI-generated intimate images are treated the same as real intimate images under Australian law.

notices.signal: Realistic images or videos of you that you know are fake surface online
notices.detail: Content showing you in situations that never happened.

notices.signal: The other person threatens to create or share deepfake content
notices.detail: They reference AI tools or tell you they can 'make' images of you.

actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner
actions.detail: Deepfake intimate images are within eSafety's remit for removal.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Creating and distributing deepfake intimate images is a criminal offence.

actions.action: Preserve evidence of the fake content and any threats
actions.detail: Screenshot everything including the source and any messages about it.

mitigations.name: Synthetic Content Reporting
mitigations.description: Report deepfake intimate content to regulatory body and police. Deepfakes treated equivalently to real NCII.

mitigations.name: Source Image Restriction
mitigations.description: Restrict access to facial photos on social media to limit deepfake source material.

detections.name: Synthetic Content Discovery
detections.description: Intimate content surfaces that depicts events that never occurred. May show AI artifacts on close inspection.

detections.name: Fabricated Content Threats
detections.description: Adversary threatens distribution of content depicting situations that never happened.

techniques.name: False Narrative Campaigns
techniques.description: Systematically spreading false information about victim to their social network, workplace, community, or online audiences. False narratives may portray victim as unstable, abusive, dishonest, or dangerous, serving to isolate victim from support, preemptively discredit their accounts of abuse, and build sympathy for perpetrator.
techniques.public_summary: Someone creates and spreads false stories about you across social media, forums, or other platforms — damaging your reputation with fabricated claims.

notices.signal: People start treating you differently based on things they've read
notices.detail: Friends, colleagues, or community members reference false claims.

notices.signal: You discover false posts or articles about you online
notices.detail: Fabricated stories appear on social media, blogs, or forums.

notices.signal: The false narrative is consistent and coordinated
notices.detail: The same lies appear across multiple platforms or from multiple accounts.

actions.action: Document all instances of the false narrative
actions.detail: Screenshot each post, note the platform, date, and URL.

actions.action: Report defamatory content to platforms
actions.detail: Most platforms prohibit false and harmful content about individuals.

actions.action: Consider legal advice about defamation
actions.detail: Persistent false narratives may constitute defamation.

actions.action: Don't engage in public arguments about the false claims
actions.detail: Responding can amplify the narrative. Focus on removal and documentation.

mitigations.name: Counter-Narrative Development
mitigations.description: Develop response strategy with support services. Share truth selectively with key contacts.

mitigations.name: False Claim Documentation
mitigations.description: Document each false claim with evidence contradicting it for legal proceedings.

detections.name: Unexplained Relationship Changes
detections.description: Contacts becoming distant without clear reason based on adversary communications.

detections.name: False Information Reports
detections.description: Trusted individuals report false information being shared by adversary.

techniques.name: Context Manipulation
techniques.description: Sharing genuine content — real messages, photos, videos, or statements — stripped of essential context to create a misleading impression of victim's character, actions, or intentions. Includes selective quoting, cropping images, sharing old content as if current, or presenting content without the circumstances that explain it.
techniques.public_summary: Someone takes your messages, posts, or content out of context — selectively sharing parts of conversations to make you look bad, or reframing your words to change their meaning.

notices.signal: People confront you about things you 'said' that feel wrong
notices.detail: Your words are being shared but the context that gave them meaning is missing.

notices.signal: Screenshots of your messages are circulating without the surrounding conversation
notices.detail: Selective quotes that change the meaning of what you wrote.

actions.action: Keep complete records of important conversations
actions.detail: Full conversation exports are harder to take out of context than isolated screenshots.

actions.action: Calmly provide the full context when confronted
actions.detail: Share the complete conversation if someone approaches you about a misleading excerpt.

actions.action: Be aware of what you put in writing
actions.detail: Not because you're doing anything wrong, but because anything can be stripped of context.

mitigations.name: Full Context Preservation
mitigations.description: Preserve complete communication threads and surrounding context.

mitigations.name: Written Communication Preference
mitigations.description: Conduct important discussions in writing on platforms maintaining complete records.

detections.name: Decontextualised Content Sharing
detections.description: Adversary shares real but misleading content stripped of surrounding context.

detections.name: Partial Truth Accusations
detections.description: Third parties confront target about statements that are technically real but misleading without context.

techniques.name: Sextortion
techniques.description: Threatening to release intimate content (real or fabricated) unless victim complies with demands for money, further intimate content, sexual acts, or other concessions. Combines elements of sexual exploitation, financial fraud, and psychological coercion, creating a cycle of escalating demands.
techniques.public_summary: Someone threatens to share intimate content unless you send money, more intimate content, or comply with other demands. This can happen with real images or fabricated content.
techniques.safety_warning: Don't pay or comply with demands. Payment doesn't stop the threats — it usually leads to more demands. Report to police immediately.

notices.signal: Someone threatens to share intimate content unless you comply
notices.detail: Demands for money, more images, or other actions.

notices.signal: Escalating demands after initial compliance
notices.detail: Giving in leads to more demands, not an end to the threats.

actions.action: Don't pay or send more content
actions.detail: Complying with demands almost never stops the threats.

actions.action: Report to police immediately
actions.detail: Sextortion is a serious criminal offence.

actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner
actions.detail: eSafety can help with removal if images are shared.

actions.action: Block the person but save all evidence first
actions.detail: Screenshot every threat, demand, and account detail before blocking.

mitigations.name: Non-Compliance
mitigations.description: Do not comply with demands. Compliance typically leads to escalating demands.

mitigations.name: Specialist Support Engagement
mitigations.description: Contact regulatory body and law enforcement sextortion support resources.

detections.name: Extortion Demands
detections.description: Messages demanding money or compliance in exchange for not distributing intimate content.

detections.name: Demand Escalation
detections.description: Increased demands following initial compliance.

techniques.name: Catfishing/Romance Fraud
techniques.description: Creating a false online identity to build a fraudulent romantic relationship with victim for purposes of financial exploitation, emotional manipulation, intelligence gathering, or other harm. May involve elaborate fake personas maintained over months or years, including stolen photos, fabricated life stories, and manufactured emotional bonds.
techniques.public_summary: Someone creates a fake online identity to form a romantic connection with you — using stolen photos and fabricated stories to build trust before exploiting it for money, information, or control.
techniques.safety_warning: If you've sent money, contact your bank immediately. There's no shame in being deceived — these operations are sophisticated and target everyone.

notices.signal: The person always has excuses for not meeting in person or video calling
notices.detail: They avoid any form of verification that would reveal their real identity.

notices.signal: The relationship moves unusually fast emotionally
notices.detail: Declarations of love, plans for the future, and emotional intensity develop very quickly.

notices.signal: Requests for money, gift cards, or financial help
notices.detail: A 'crisis' emerges that requires your financial help.

actions.action: Reverse image search their photos
actions.detail: Use Google Images or TinEye to check if their photos appear elsewhere online under different names.

actions.action: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person
actions.detail: Legitimate romantic interests don't need emergency funds from people they've never met.

actions.action: Report to the platform and to Scamwatch
actions.detail: Report at scamwatch.gov.au.

actions.action: Contact your bank if you've sent money
actions.detail: They may be able to recover or stop transfers.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.description: Verify online relationship identity through video calls and reverse image search before trust development.

mitigations.name: Financial Boundary Enforcement
mitigations.description: Never send money or financial information to online-only contacts.

detections.name: Verification Avoidance
detections.description: Person consistently avoids video calls or in-person meetings. Photos may belong to someone else.

detections.name: Financial Request Escalation
detections.description: Increasingly urgent requests for financial assistance with compelling stories.

techniques.name: Reputation Destruction SEO
techniques.description: Creating websites, blog posts, social media content, or other material specifically designed to rank highly in search results for victim's name, damaging their reputation to anyone who searches for them. Content may include false accusations, embarrassing information, intimate images, or misleading narratives.
techniques.public_title: Destroying Your Reputation in Search Results
techniques.public_summary: Someone creates websites, posts, or content specifically designed to appear in search results for your name — filling the first page of Google with damaging, false, or embarrassing content about you.

notices.signal: Searching your name returns harmful content you didn't create
notices.detail: Negative posts, fake profiles, or defamatory content ranks in search results.

notices.signal: New websites or pages about you appear that you didn't make
notices.detail: Deliberately created content designed to damage your reputation.

actions.action: Document all harmful search results
actions.detail: Screenshot and save URLs of content that appears in search results for your name.

actions.action: Request removal from Google
actions.detail: Google has a process for removing certain types of harmful personal information from search results.

actions.action: Consider professional reputation management
actions.detail: SEO specialists can help push harmful content lower in search results.

actions.action: Report defamatory content to hosting platforms
actions.detail: Request removal of false and harmful content.

mitigations.name: Search Result Monitoring
mitigations.description: Set up alerts for own name. Regular self-search to identify harmful content early.

mitigations.name: Positive Content Creation
mitigations.description: Create professional content under own name to influence search results.

mitigations.name: Legal Content Removal
mitigations.description: Seek legal advice about defamation action or court-ordered content removal.

detections.name: Harmful Search Results
detections.description: Name search reveals websites containing false or harmful content designed to rank highly.

detections.name: Malicious Domain Registrations
detections.description: Websites registered using target's name containing harmful content.

techniques.name: Historical Content Weaponization
techniques.description: Surfacing old posts, photos, messages, or other historical digital content to harm victim in their current context. Includes finding embarrassing teenage posts, old dating profiles, past political statements, or previously private content that can be taken out of context to damage victim's current relationships, employment, or reputation.
techniques.public_title: Digging Up Old Content to Use Against You
techniques.public_summary: Someone searches through your digital history — old social media posts, archived content, or past online activity — to find things that can be used to embarrass, discredit, or blackmail you.

notices.signal: Old posts or content you'd forgotten about resurface
notices.detail: Things from years ago are suddenly being shared or referenced.

notices.signal: The other person references content from deep in your history
notices.detail: They've clearly spent time searching through your past.

actions.action: Review and clean up old social media posts
actions.detail: Most platforms let you delete or hide old posts. Consider a privacy review of your history.

actions.action: Check what's visible on web archives
actions.detail: Sites like the Wayback Machine may have cached old content.

actions.action: Adjust privacy settings on past content
actions.detail: Many platforms allow you to change the audience on old posts retroactively.

mitigations.name: Historical Content Cleanup
mitigations.description: Review and restrict visibility of old content that could be weaponised.

mitigations.name: Context Preparation
mitigations.description: Prepare contextual explanations for known historical content with support team.

detections.name: Old Content Resurfacing
detections.description: Historical content shared in new contexts timed to important events.

detections.name: Content Archiving Activity
detections.description: Evidence adversary systematically archiving target's historical content.

techniques.name: Fake Evidence Creation
techniques.description: Fabricating digital evidence including fake emails, text messages, documents, receipts, screenshots, or records to frame victim for misconduct, support false legal claims, or manipulate decision-makers. May involve sophisticated forgeries using editing tools or simple fabrication of documents.
techniques.public_summary: Someone fabricates digital evidence — fake messages, edited screenshots, forged documents, or manipulated records — to use against you in legal proceedings, custody disputes, or to manipulate others.
techniques.safety_warning: If you suspect fake evidence is being used against you in legal proceedings, tell your lawyer immediately. Digital forensics can often prove fabrication.

notices.signal: Evidence presented against you doesn't match your records
notices.detail: Screenshots, messages, or documents that don't match what actually happened.

notices.signal: The timing, formatting, or details of 'evidence' seem off
notices.detail: Metadata, fonts, or platform formatting don't look right.

actions.action: Keep your own independent records of all important interactions
actions.detail: Your records are your protection against fabrication.

actions.action: Tell your lawyer about suspected fake evidence immediately
actions.detail: Legal professionals can engage digital forensics experts to examine evidence.

actions.action: Don't accuse the other person of fabrication without evidence
actions.detail: Let the forensic evidence speak for itself in legal settings.

actions.action: Preserve originals of all communications
actions.detail: Export full conversation logs rather than relying on screenshots.

mitigations.name: Digital Forensic Engagement
mitigations.description: Engage forensic specialist to analyse suspected fabricated evidence and provide expert testimony.

mitigations.name: Platform Record Requests
mitigations.description: Request official platform records for critical communications. Harder to fabricate than screenshots.

detections.name: Evidence Inconsistent with Records
detections.description: Presented evidence doesn't match target's records or memory of events.

detections.name: Metadata Inconsistencies
detections.description: Digital evidence contains impossible timestamps, missing metadata, or editing artifacts.

techniques.name: Communication Interception & Response
techniques.description: Reading and responding to victim's messages while impersonating the victim, without their knowledge. Perpetrator intercepts communications from victim's friends, family, support services, or legal representatives and responds as the victim, undermining support networks and controlling information flow.
techniques.public_title: Reading & Replying to Your Messages as You
techniques.public_summary: Someone reads your messages from friends, family, or support services — and responds pretending to be you, without your knowledge. This isolates you by undermining your relationships and cutting off support.
techniques.safety_warning: If someone is intercepting your messages, people trying to help you may be receiving false responses. Consider reaching out through a completely different channel.

notices.signal: Friends or family mention conversations you don't remember having
notices.detail: People reference messages 'you' sent that you didn't write.

notices.signal: Support services or lawyers say you declined help or cancelled appointments
notices.detail: Someone responded on your behalf to turn away support.

notices.signal: Relationships deteriorate for reasons you can't understand
notices.detail: People seem hurt or confused by interactions that didn't happen from your side.

actions.action: Tell trusted people about the interception
actions.detail: Explain that messages from your accounts may not be from you. Establish a verification method.

actions.action: Use a separate, secure communication channel
actions.detail: A new phone, a new email, or an in-person visit to re-establish contact with key people.

actions.action: Check your accounts for unauthorised access
actions.detail: Review active sessions and change passwords from a safe device.

mitigations.name: Secure Communication Channel
mitigations.description: Use separate secure device for sensitive communications with support services.

mitigations.name: Message Verification
mitigations.description: Verify directly with contacts if relationships deteriorate unexpectedly.

detections.name: Unauthorised Message Sending
detections.description: Contacts report receiving messages from target's accounts not sent by target.

detections.name: Unexplained Relationship Deterioration
detections.description: Support relationships deteriorate without clear cause.

techniques.name: Contact Blocking/Filtering
techniques.description: Blocking victim's contacts or filtering their incoming communications without victim's knowledge or consent. Perpetrator may block specific people on victim's phone, set up email filters to auto-delete messages from support contacts, or manipulate device settings to prevent certain calls or messages from reaching victim.
techniques.public_title: Blocking Your Contacts Without Your Knowledge
techniques.public_summary: Someone blocks phone numbers, email addresses, or social media connections on your devices — so messages from friends, family, or services never reach you, and you don't know they tried.

notices.signal: People say they tried to contact you but you never received the messages
notices.detail: Friends, family, or services report messages and calls going unanswered.

notices.signal: You feel increasingly isolated without understanding why
notices.detail: People seem to have stopped reaching out, but they actually haven't.

notices.signal: Blocked contact lists on your phone contain numbers you didn't block
notices.detail: Check your device's blocked contacts list for unexpected entries.

actions.action: Regularly check your blocked contacts and email filters
actions.detail: On iPhone: Settings > Phone > Blocked Contacts. Check email spam/filter rules too.

actions.action: Ask trusted people to test whether their messages reach you
actions.detail: A simple 'did you get my text?' check can reveal blocking.

actions.action: Use a secondary contact method for critical relationships
actions.detail: Give key people an alternate way to reach you if your primary phone seems unreliable.

mitigations.name: Contact and Filter Audit
mitigations.description: Periodically check blocked contacts and email filter rules for unauthorised changes.

mitigations.name: Alternative Contact Methods
mitigations.description: Maintain backup contact methods for key support people.

detections.name: Missing Inbound Communications
detections.description: Contacts report sending messages that were never received.

detections.name: Unauthorised Blocked Contacts
detections.description: Contacts on blocked list that user did not block.

techniques.name: Social Media Control
techniques.description: Controlling who victim can follow, friend, interact with, or be visible to on social media platforms. May involve demanding victim unfriend specific contacts, monitoring follower/following lists, requiring approval before posting, or demanding social media passwords to vet all interactions.
techniques.public_summary: Someone controls who you can follow, what you can post, or who can contact you on social media — either by demanding you change settings, by accessing your accounts, or through constant monitoring that makes you self-censor.

notices.signal: You feel you can't post freely because the other person will react
notices.detail: Fear of the other person's response controls what you share online.

notices.signal: The other person dictates who you can follow or be friends with online
notices.detail: They demand you remove connections or restrict your social media activity.

notices.signal: Your social media settings have been changed without your input
notices.detail: Privacy settings, friend lists, or profile information has been altered.

actions.action: Recognise that controlling your social media is controlling behaviour
actions.detail: You have the right to use social media freely.

actions.action: Create a private account the other person doesn't know about
actions.detail: A separate space where you can communicate freely.
actions.safety_note: Use a different email and don't link it to your primary accounts.

actions.action: Talk to someone you trust about what's happening
actions.detail: Controlling behaviour escalates. Getting support early matters.

mitigations.name: Autonomy Assertion
mitigations.description: Recognise demands to control social media connections as controlling behaviour. Document demands.

mitigations.name: Private Secondary Account
mitigations.description: Maintain separate private account for support connections if needed.

detections.name: Connection Control Demands
detections.description: Demands to unfriend specific people, restrict posting, or delete accounts.

detections.name: Connection Monitoring
detections.description: Adversary comments on or confronts about social media connections and interactions.

techniques.name: Device Time/Access Restrictions
techniques.description: Using parental controls, screen time management, MDM features, or physical control to restrict when and how victim can use their own devices. Limits victim's ability to communicate, access information, seek help, or maintain independence.
techniques.public_summary: Someone controls when and how you can use your phone, computer, or internet — imposing time limits, taking your devices, or restricting your access to technology.
techniques.safety_warning: Controlling someone's access to communication technology is a form of coercive control. In Australia, this can be a criminal offence.

notices.signal: The other person takes your phone or controls when you can use it
notices.detail: Your access to devices is rationed or conditional.

notices.signal: Parental control software is installed on your devices (when you're an adult)
notices.detail: Screen time limits or content restrictions are applied to your devices without your consent.

notices.signal: Internet access is turned off as punishment or control
notices.detail: Wi-Fi passwords are changed, routers are unplugged, or data is restricted.

actions.action: Identify a safe communication method the other person can't control
actions.detail: A device at work, a trusted friend's phone, or a library computer.

actions.action: Remove parental control profiles from your devices
actions.detail: These should not be on an adult's device without their consent.
actions.safety_note: The other person may be notified.

actions.action: Talk to a support service
actions.detail: Call 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) from a safe phone. Controlling access to technology is recognised as abuse.

mitigations.name: Parental Control Removal
mitigations.description: Remove parental controls from adult devices. Factory reset if removal not possible.

mitigations.name: Secondary Device Access
mitigations.description: Maintain access to secondary device adversary cannot control.

detections.name: External Device Restrictions
detections.description: Device has time limits, app restrictions, or content filters not configured by user.

detections.name: Resource Access Blocking
detections.description: Support websites, apps, or communication tools blocked at device or network level.

techniques.name: Network Poisoning
techniques.description: Contacting victim's support network (friends, family, colleagues, therapist, legal counsel) to spread lies, create conflict, or undermine trust. Perpetrator strategically reaches out to key support people to isolate victim from help sources, often preemptively positioning themselves as the reasonable party.
techniques.public_summary: Someone contacts your friends, family, colleagues, or community to spread lies about you — turning your support network against you so you have nowhere to turn.

notices.signal: People in your life are distancing themselves based on false information
notices.detail: Relationships change because of things the other person has told them.

notices.signal: The other person contacts your friends, family, or workplace
notices.detail: They reach out to people in your life under various pretexts.

notices.signal: Your reputation within your community shifts without explanation
notices.detail: People treat you differently based on a narrative you didn't create.

actions.action: Talk directly to the people who matter
actions.detail: Have honest conversations with close friends and family about what's happening.

actions.action: Keep records of what the other person tells people
actions.detail: If you learn about specific lies, document them.

actions.action: Don't try to counter every lie
actions.detail: Focus on your closest relationships. You can't control everyone's perception.

mitigations.name: Support Network Communication
mitigations.description: Proactively inform key contacts about adversary's potential false information campaign.

mitigations.name: Professional Support Briefing
mitigations.description: Ensure professionals (therapist, lawyer, caseworker) are aware adversary may contact them.

detections.name: Contact Attitude Changes
detections.description: Contacts suddenly withdrawing support or becoming hostile based on adversary communications.

detections.name: Adversary Contact Reports
detections.description: Support people report adversary has contacted them.

techniques.name: Platform Banning Coordination
techniques.description: Orchestrating victim's removal or banning from online platforms, groups, or communities where they have established support networks. Uses coordinated mass reporting, false claims of terms of service violations, or manipulation of community moderators to silence and isolate victim.
techniques.public_summary: Someone coordinates false reports to get your accounts suspended or banned from platforms you rely on — for work, social connection, or accessing services.

notices.signal: Your accounts are suspended for violations you didn't commit
notices.detail: Bans or restrictions appear after waves of false reports.

notices.signal: Multiple platform bans happen in a short period
notices.detail: Coordinated reporting across platforms.

actions.action: Appeal every suspension
actions.detail: Platforms have appeal processes. Use them and explain the pattern of false reporting.

actions.action: Document the pattern across platforms
actions.detail: Evidence of coordinated false reporting strengthens your case.

actions.action: Contact platform trust and safety teams directly
actions.detail: Explain the situation and request protection for your accounts.

mitigations.name: Ban Appeal with Context
mitigations.description: Appeal bans with context about coordinated reporting campaign.

mitigations.name: Support Network Diversification
mitigations.description: Maintain connections across multiple platforms and in-person support.

detections.name: Unexplained Community Removal
detections.description: Banned from communities without clear policy violation.

detections.name: Coordinated Reporting Evidence
detections.description: Community administrators report multiple reports received in short timeframe.

techniques.name: Communication Monitoring Disclosure
techniques.description: Deliberately telling victim that all their communications are being monitored to create a chilling effect of self-censorship. Victim becomes afraid to reach out for help, discuss the abuse, or communicate honestly, effectively isolating themselves out of fear. May be truthful or bluffed.
techniques.public_summary: Someone tells you they're monitoring everything you say and do online — creating a chilling effect where you're afraid to reach out for help, talk to friends, or communicate freely.
techniques.safety_warning: Even if the monitoring claims are exaggerated or false, the fear they create is real. Reach out for help through a channel you believe is safe.

notices.signal: The other person explicitly tells you they can see everything
notices.detail: Statements like 'I know everything you do' or 'I can read all your messages'.

notices.signal: You self-censor everything because you assume you're watched
notices.detail: Fear of surveillance prevents you from seeking help.

notices.signal: The other person demonstrates knowledge that seems to prove monitoring
notices.detail: They may have some access, but use it to imply total surveillance.

actions.action: Understand that total monitoring is very difficult
actions.detail: Most people can't actually see everything. The claim is often bigger than the reality.

actions.action: Find one safe way to communicate
actions.detail: Even one unmonitored channel — a friend's phone, an in-person conversation — is enough to start getting help.

actions.action: Contact 1800RESPECT from a safe phone
actions.detail: They can help you assess how much monitoring is actually happening and make a safety plan.

mitigations.name: Monitoring Assumption Planning
mitigations.description: Use separate safe device for sensitive communications if monitoring disclosed.

mitigations.name: Monitoring Capability Verification
mitigations.description: Have professional assess actual monitoring capability to calibrate response.

detections.name: Explicit Monitoring Claims
detections.description: Adversary states they can monitor communications, either as threat or demonstrated through knowledge.

detections.name: Self-Censorship Behaviour
detections.description: Target stops seeking help or being honest in communications due to monitoring fear.

techniques.name: Support Resource Blocking
techniques.description: Blocking victim's access to helplines, support websites, crisis services, legal aid resources, or domestic violence organizations. May involve website blocking through router controls, removing helpline numbers from victim's phone, or intercepting communications with support services.
techniques.public_title: Blocking Your Access to Help Services
techniques.public_summary: Someone blocks your access to support services — helpline numbers, support websites, counselling services, or legal aid — so you can't get help.
techniques.safety_warning: If someone is blocking your access to support services, that is a serious form of coercive control. Find any way you can to reach help.

notices.signal: Helpline numbers or support websites don't work from your devices
notices.detail: Numbers may be blocked, or websites may be filtered.

notices.signal: The other person discourages you from seeking help
notices.detail: They tell you services won't help, or that calling will make things worse.

notices.signal: Contact details for services have been deleted from your phone
notices.detail: Saved numbers or bookmarks for support services disappear.

actions.action: Memorise key numbers: 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732), 000 for emergencies
actions.detail: Numbers you know by heart can't be deleted from your phone.

actions.action: Access support from a different device or location
actions.detail: A library, a friend's phone, or your workplace.

actions.action: Ask someone you trust to make the call for you
actions.detail: If you can't safely call, someone else can.

mitigations.name: Alternative Resource Access
mitigations.description: Memorise key helpline numbers. Use mobile data or public computers to access blocked resources.

mitigations.name: Network Blocking Bypass
mitigations.description: Use mobile data, change DNS settings, or use VPN to bypass network-level blocking.

detections.name: Support Website Inaccessibility
detections.description: Support resources inaccessible on home network but work on mobile data.

detections.name: Support Contact Removal
detections.description: Helpline numbers or support bookmarks removed from devices without user action.

techniques.name: Identity Document Control
techniques.description: Controlling access to digital copies of victim's important identification documents including passport scans, birth certificates, tax records, medical records, immigration documents, or legal paperwork. Restricts victim's ability to access services, prove identity, or leave the relationship.
techniques.public_summary: Someone takes control of your digital identity documents — passwords, Medicare, tax accounts, licences — making it difficult to access services, travel, or prove your identity.
techniques.safety_warning: Loss of identity documents can make it very difficult to access services or leave an unsafe situation. Government agencies can help you recover access.

notices.signal: You can't access your myGov, tax, Medicare, or other government accounts
notices.detail: Passwords have been changed or your accounts have been linked to the other person's.

notices.signal: The other person holds all the important account credentials
notices.detail: You don't know the passwords to your own identity-related accounts.

notices.signal: Your mail is being redirected or intercepted
notices.detail: Important documents and correspondence aren't reaching you.

actions.action: Contact Services Australia to regain access to myGov
actions.detail: They can verify your identity and help you recover your account.

actions.action: Visit a government service centre in person with photo ID
actions.detail: In-person identity verification can bypass compromised online accounts.

actions.action: Set up a PO Box or redirect mail to a safe address
actions.detail: Ensure important documents reach you.

mitigations.name: Document Duplication
mitigations.description: Obtain copies of critical identity documents. Store in adversary-inaccessible location.

mitigations.name: Government Portal Security
mitigations.description: Secure access to government portals under sole-controlled credentials.

detections.name: Document Access Denial
detections.description: Cannot access digital identity documents due to adversary-controlled storage.

detections.name: Document Relocation
detections.description: Digital documents moved, deleted, or password-protected without user action.

techniques.name: Email/Communication Rerouting
techniques.description: Setting up email forwarding rules, message redirects, or call forwarding to intercept victim's incoming communications without their knowledge. Allows perpetrator to monitor all communications and selectively prevent messages from reaching victim, particularly from support services or legal representatives.
techniques.public_summary: Someone sets up forwarding rules on your email or messaging accounts so copies of everything you receive are also sent to them — or so that certain messages are redirected and never reach you.

notices.signal: You're not receiving messages or emails you're expecting
notices.detail: People tell you they sent things you never received.

notices.signal: Email forwarding or filtering rules you didn't create
notices.detail: Check your email settings for unexpected forwarding addresses or filter rules.

notices.signal: The other person knows about emails or messages you received
notices.detail: They reference content from messages sent to you.

actions.action: Check email forwarding and filter rules immediately
actions.detail: Gmail: Settings > Forwarding. Also check Filters and Blocked Addresses.

actions.action: Check app-specific forwarding
actions.detail: WhatsApp Web, Telegram sessions, and other apps may have active sessions forwarding your messages.

actions.action: Change email passwords and review all connected apps
actions.detail: Remove any third-party app access you don't recognise.

mitigations.name: Forwarding Rule Audit
mitigations.description: Check email settings for unauthorised forwarding rules and filters.

mitigations.name: Call Forwarding Check
mitigations.description: Check phone settings and carrier account for call forwarding configurations.

detections.name: Missing Expected Communications
detections.description: Emails, messages, or calls that senders confirm were sent but never received.

detections.name: Forwarding Discovery
detections.description: Audit reveals email forwarding or call forwarding to unknown destinations.

techniques.name: Financial Account Lockout
techniques.description: Changing passwords, removing authorized users, or otherwise denying victim access to shared or individual financial accounts. Cuts victim off from their own money, savings, investments, or financial records, creating immediate economic vulnerability and dependence.
techniques.public_title: Locking You Out of Your Money
techniques.public_summary: Someone locks you out of bank accounts, credit cards, or financial services — changing passwords, removing your access, or freezing accounts you depend on.
techniques.safety_warning: If you've been locked out of your bank accounts, contact your bank directly. Financial abuse is taken seriously by financial institutions.

notices.signal: You can't access online banking or financial accounts
notices.detail: Passwords have been changed or your access has been revoked.

notices.signal: Cards are cancelled or frozen without your knowledge
notices.detail: Your cards stop working unexpectedly.

notices.signal: The other person controls all financial account access
notices.detail: You have no independent access to money.

actions.action: Contact your bank directly, in person or by phone
actions.detail: Explain the situation. Banks have processes for domestic and family violence situations.

actions.action: Open an account in your name only
actions.detail: A separate account the other person doesn't know about provides financial safety.

actions.action: Ask about the bank's DFV support services
actions.detail: Most Australian banks have dedicated domestic and family violence teams.

mitigations.name: Financial Account Security Reset
mitigations.description: Change passwords, enable MFA, remove adversary as authorised user on individual accounts.

mitigations.name: Financial Counselling
mitigations.description: Contact financial counsellor experienced in DFV situations for guidance.

mitigations.name: Emergency Financial Access
mitigations.description: Maintain separate emergency fund in adversary-unknown account.

detections.name: Financial Account Lockout
detections.description: Unable to access financial accounts using previously valid credentials.

detections.name: Authorised User Removal
detections.description: Notification of removal from shared financial accounts.

techniques.name: Transaction Monitoring
techniques.description: Tracking all of victim's financial transactions through shared bank account access, transaction alert notifications, statement monitoring, or financial app access. Creates comprehensive surveillance of victim's spending, location (from merchant addresses), social activities, and any attempts to prepare for leaving.
techniques.public_summary: Someone monitors every transaction you make — tracking where you shop, what you buy, and how you spend money through shared bank accounts, linked cards, or transaction notifications.

notices.signal: The other person questions purchases they shouldn't know about
notices.detail: They reference specific transactions from your account.

notices.signal: You feel unable to make any purchase without scrutiny
notices.detail: Every dollar is monitored and questioned.

notices.signal: Transaction notifications are going to the other person's device
notices.detail: Alerts for your spending are being received by them.

actions.action: Open a separate account for independent spending
actions.detail: Even small amounts of independent money provide freedom.

actions.action: Check notification settings on banking apps
actions.detail: Remove the other person's device from transaction alerts.

actions.action: Use cash for sensitive purchases when safe to do so
actions.detail: Cash transactions don't create digital records.

mitigations.name: Separate Transaction Account
mitigations.description: Open individual account at different institution for sensitive transactions.

mitigations.name: Untraceable Payment Methods
mitigations.description: Use cash or prepaid cards for purchases to keep private.

detections.name: Transaction Knowledge
detections.description: Adversary references specific purchases, amounts, or merchants from bank transactions.

detections.name: Unauthorised Alert Configuration
detections.description: Transaction alerts configured to adversary's contact information.

techniques.name: Spending Restrictions
techniques.description: Using account controls, card limits, transaction blocks, or approval requirements to restrict what victim can spend money on, how much, and where. May exploit joint account features, parental controls on youth accounts applied to adults, or business account administrative features.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses technology to restrict your spending — setting limits on cards, requiring approval for purchases, or controlling access to money through banking apps.

notices.signal: Your card is declined for purchases you should be able to make
notices.detail: Spending limits have been set without your agreement.

notices.signal: You need to request or justify every purchase
notices.detail: The other person requires approval before you can spend.

notices.signal: Restrictions change based on the other person's mood or as punishment
notices.detail: Your access to money is used as a tool of control.

actions.action: Contact your bank about your rights to your own accounts
actions.detail: You have legal rights to accounts in your name.

actions.action: Build independent financial access gradually
actions.detail: A separate account, even with small amounts, creates options.

actions.action: Seek financial counselling
actions.detail: Free financial counselling services can help you plan for financial independence.

mitigations.name: Independent Financial Access
mitigations.description: Establish independent financial access: personal account, credit card, superannuation access.

mitigations.name: Legal Financial Advice
mitigations.description: Consult lawyer about financial rights and emergency relief options.

detections.name: Unexplained Transaction Declines
detections.description: Card declined despite available funds, or daily limits reduced without consent.

detections.name: Spending Approval Requirements
detections.description: Spending limits or approval requirements enabled without user action.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Transactions
techniques.description: Making purchases, transfers, or withdrawals from victim's financial accounts without consent. May drain savings, make extravagant purchases, transfer funds to perpetrator-controlled accounts, or take on debt in victim's name. Often escalates during separation when perpetrator seeks to deplete shared resources.
techniques.public_summary: Someone makes purchases, transfers, or financial transactions using your accounts or cards without your knowledge or consent.

notices.signal: Unexplained transactions on your accounts
notices.detail: Purchases, transfers, or withdrawals you didn't make.

notices.signal: Your account balance is lower than expected
notices.detail: Money is leaving your account without your knowledge.

notices.signal: Subscriptions or payments set up without your consent
notices.detail: Recurring charges you didn't authorise.

actions.action: Report unauthorised transactions to your bank immediately
actions.detail: Banks can reverse fraudulent transactions and secure your account.

actions.action: Change your banking passwords and PINs
actions.detail: Do this from a safe device.

actions.action: Request new cards with new numbers
actions.detail: This stops any saved card details from being reused.

mitigations.name: Transaction Alert Configuration
mitigations.description: Enable real-time transaction alerts on all financial accounts.

mitigations.name: Fraud Reporting
mitigations.description: Report unauthorised transactions to financial institution and police.

detections.name: Unrecognised Transactions
detections.description: Transactions appearing on accounts not authorised by account holder.

detections.name: Balance Discrepancies
detections.description: Account balances lower than expected or funds moved without knowledge.

techniques.name: Coerced Transactions
techniques.description: Using threats, intimidation, or manipulation to force victim to transfer money, sign financial documents, take on debt, or make purchases. Digital coercion may include threatening messages, threatening to share intimate images, threatening custody action, or other leverage to compel financial compliance.
techniques.public_title: Forcing You to Make Financial Decisions
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses threats, pressure, or manipulation to force you to sign contracts, take out loans, transfer money, or make financial decisions that benefit them and harm you.
techniques.safety_warning: Coerced financial transactions may be voidable under law. Talk to a lawyer — many legal aid services offer free advice.

notices.signal: You've been pressured into signing documents or making transfers
notices.detail: Financial decisions made under duress or threat.

notices.signal: Debts or loans in your name that primarily benefit the other person
notices.detail: You're legally responsible for obligations that serve them.

actions.action: Seek legal advice about coerced transactions
actions.detail: Legal aid services can advise on whether transactions can be reversed.

actions.action: Contact your bank and explain the coercion
actions.detail: Banks have processes for domestic and family violence situations.

actions.action: Keep evidence of the pressure or threats
actions.detail: Messages, recordings, or witness statements documenting the coercion.

mitigations.name: Coerced Debt Legal Advice
mitigations.description: Consult about coerced debt pathways. Debts incurred under duress may be dischargeable.

mitigations.name: Coercion Documentation
mitigations.description: Document coercion circumstances for legal proceedings.

detections.name: Financial Coercion
detections.description: Threats, intimidation, or manipulation to make transactions or take on debt.

detections.name: Duress Debt Accumulation
detections.description: Increasing debt from pressured financial decisions.

techniques.name: Crypto/Investment Fraud
techniques.description: Deceiving victim into fraudulent cryptocurrency investments, fake trading platforms, or other financial schemes. Often involves building trust, demonstrating fake returns, and gradually escalating investment amounts. May also involve coerced cryptocurrency transfers that are difficult to trace or recover.
techniques.public_summary: Someone manipulates you into investing money in fake cryptocurrency schemes, fraudulent investments, or scam platforms — often through a romantic relationship or trusted connection.
techniques.safety_warning: If you've invested money in a scheme you now suspect is fraudulent, contact your bank and report to Scamwatch immediately.

notices.signal: Investment 'returns' exist only on screen, not as withdrawable money
notices.detail: You can see profits on a platform but can't actually withdraw them.

notices.signal: Pressure to invest more, especially after initial 'gains'
notices.detail: The scheme requires increasing investment.

notices.signal: The other person is unusually knowledgeable about your investment decisions
notices.detail: They guide you to specific platforms or trades.

actions.action: Stop investing immediately if you suspect fraud
actions.detail: Don't send more money to recover losses.

actions.action: Report to Scamwatch at scamwatch.gov.au
actions.detail: Report the scheme to help protect others.

actions.action: Contact your bank about recovering funds
actions.detail: Quick action may help recover some money.

mitigations.name: Investment Verification
mitigations.description: Verify investment opportunities independently through regulatory body resources.

mitigations.name: Fraud Reporting
mitigations.description: Report suspected investment fraud to consumer protection and cyber security agencies.

detections.name: Pressure to Invest in Unverified Platforms
detections.description: Urged to invest on unfamiliar platforms that cannot be independently verified.

detections.name: Withdrawal Inability
detections.description: Invested funds cannot be withdrawn from platform.

techniques.name: Benefits/Payments Interception
techniques.description: Redirecting victim's income, government benefits, tax refunds, insurance payments, or other financial entitlements to perpetrator-controlled accounts. May involve changing direct deposit information, intercepting physical mail, controlling online government portals, or filing fraudulent claims.
techniques.public_summary: Someone intercepts, redirects, or controls your government payments — including Centrelink, child support, or other benefits — by changing account details or controlling your myGov access.
techniques.safety_warning: If your government payments are being intercepted, contact Services Australia directly.

notices.signal: Centrelink or other payments aren't arriving in your account
notices.detail: Payments have been redirected to a different bank account.

notices.signal: The other person controls your myGov or Centrelink access
notices.detail: You can't log in to manage your own payments.

actions.action: Contact Services Australia directly
actions.detail: Visit in person or call. They can verify your identity and restore your access.

actions.action: Request payments go to an account only you control
actions.detail: Open a new bank account if needed.

actions.action: Ask about a social worker at Centrelink
actions.detail: They can provide additional support for domestic violence situations.

mitigations.name: Payment Destination Security
mitigations.description: Ensure all payments directed to sole-controlled account. Update payment details with agencies and employers.

mitigations.name: Mail Redirection Check
mitigations.description: Verify no mail redirection configured without knowledge.

detections.name: Missing Expected Payments
detections.description: Government benefits, salary, or other payments not arriving in expected accounts.

detections.name: Payment Detail Changes
detections.description: Direct deposit information changed without authorisation.

techniques.name: Credit/Identity Theft
techniques.description: Opening financial accounts, taking on debt, applying for credit, or conducting financial transactions using victim's personal information and identity without consent. Damages victim's credit score, creates legal liability, and may take years to resolve. Often not discovered until victim is denied credit or contacted by collectors.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses your personal information to open accounts, take out loans, or incur debts in your name — damaging your credit history and creating financial obligations you didn't agree to.

notices.signal: Bills or statements arrive for accounts you didn't open
notices.detail: Credit cards, loans, or services in your name that you didn't apply for.

notices.signal: Your credit score has dropped unexpectedly
notices.detail: Debts you didn't incur are affecting your credit.

notices.signal: Debt collectors contact you about debts you don't recognise
notices.detail: Obligations in your name that aren't yours.

actions.action: Check your credit report
actions.detail: You can get a free credit report from Equifax, Experian, or illion.

actions.action: Report identity theft to IDCARE (1800 595 160)
actions.detail: IDCARE is Australia's national identity and cyber support service.

actions.action: Place a ban on your credit file
