actions.detail: This prevents new credit from being opened in your name.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Identity theft and fraud are criminal offences.

mitigations.name: Credit Monitoring
mitigations.description: Set up credit monitoring. Request credit reports from all reporting bodies.

mitigations.name: Credit Ban
mitigations.description: Place credit ban to prevent new applications. Available free for DFV victims.

mitigations.name: Identity Theft Report
mitigations.description: Report identity theft to national identity support service.

detections.name: Unknown Credit Activity
detections.description: Credit report shows accounts or enquiries not initiated by owner.

detections.name: Unknown Service Bills
detections.description: Bills or collection notices for services never subscribed to.

techniques.name: Smart Home Resource Control
techniques.description: Controlling heating, cooling, electricity, water, locks, lighting, or other utilities through smart home systems to coerce, punish, or make the home environment hostile. Perpetrator with administrative access can remotely control living conditions, creating physical discomfort or danger.
techniques.public_title: Controlling Your Home Through Smart Devices
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses smart home technology to control your living environment — changing heating/cooling, locking/unlocking doors, turning utilities on and off, or creating an uncomfortable or unsafe home.
techniques.safety_warning: If smart home devices are being used to create unsafe conditions (extreme temperatures, locked doors), contact police.

notices.signal: Temperature, lighting, or appliances change without your input
notices.detail: The heating turns off in winter, or lights turn on and off at night.

notices.signal: Smart locks change codes or lock you in/out
notices.detail: You can't get in or out of your home, or the codes keep changing.

notices.signal: The other person controls these devices remotely after separation
notices.detail: They retain admin access to home systems after moving out.

actions.action: Identify who controls the smart home accounts
actions.detail: Determine which devices are connected and who has admin access.

actions.action: Factory reset smart home devices
actions.detail: This removes all previous connections. Set them up fresh.
actions.safety_note: The other person may notice devices going offline.

actions.action: Contact your utility providers to separate accounts
actions.detail: Ensure you have independent control of electricity, gas, and internet.

mitigations.name: Smart Home Account Control
mitigations.description: Transfer all smart home device accounts to sole control. Factory reset and reconfigure.

mitigations.name: Manual Override Capability
mitigations.description: Ensure manual overrides available for all smart home-controlled utilities.

detections.name: Remote Utility Control
detections.description: Heating, cooling, lighting, or locks changing without user action.

detections.name: Manipulation-Reflective Utility Bills
detections.description: Unusual utility bills resulting from remote environmental manipulation.

techniques.name: Employment Sabotage
techniques.description: Interfering with victim's employment through manipulation of work communications, sending messages to employers, sabotaging job applications, damaging professional online presence, or disrupting work-related accounts. Aims to undermine victim's economic independence and professional reputation.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses technology to undermine your employment — sending messages to your employer, interfering with your work accounts, making you miss meetings, or damaging your professional reputation.

notices.signal: Your employer receives messages or information about you from the other person
notices.detail: They contact your workplace to cause problems.

notices.signal: Work accounts are interfered with
notices.detail: You miss meetings, deadlines, or communications due to sabotage.

notices.signal: Your professional reputation is being damaged online
notices.detail: LinkedIn, professional directories, or industry forums are targeted.

actions.action: Tell your employer what's happening
actions.detail: Many workplaces have policies for supporting employees experiencing domestic violence.

actions.action: Secure your work accounts independently
actions.detail: Change passwords and enable 2FA on all work-related accounts.

actions.action: Document the sabotage
actions.detail: Keep records of every interference for HR and potentially for legal action.

mitigations.name: Employer Notification
mitigations.description: Inform employer about potential for adversary workplace contact if safe to do so.

mitigations.name: Professional Account Security
mitigations.description: Secure professional accounts with strong credentials and MFA.

detections.name: Workplace Interference
detections.description: Employer or colleagues report contact from adversary about target.

detections.name: Application Interference
detections.description: Job applications unsuccessful potentially due to adversary contact with prospective employers.

techniques.name: Subscription/Service Cancellation
techniques.description: Cancelling victim's essential services including phone plans, internet service, insurance, utility accounts, or subscriptions without consent. Disrupts victim's daily life, communication ability, and access to essential services. May be timed to cause maximum impact such as during extreme weather or when victim is isolated.
techniques.public_summary: Someone cancels your subscriptions, services, or utilities — phone plan, internet, streaming, insurance, or other services you depend on — to disrupt your life and assert control.

notices.signal: Services stop working unexpectedly
notices.detail: Your phone, internet, or other services are disconnected.

notices.signal: You receive cancellation confirmations you didn't request
notices.detail: Services you rely on have been cancelled.

notices.signal: The other person has account access to services in your name
notices.detail: They can make changes because they know the login details.

actions.action: Contact service providers to secure your accounts
actions.detail: Add passwords or PINs that only you know.

actions.action: Set up essential services in your own name with your own credentials
actions.detail: Independent accounts can't be cancelled by someone else.

actions.action: Document cancelled services and the impact
actions.detail: This evidence may be relevant for legal proceedings.

mitigations.name: Individual Account Registration
mitigations.description: Register essential services under own name and billing.

mitigations.name: Service Provider DFV Support
mitigations.description: Request DFV support pathway from service providers for expedited account changes.

detections.name: Essential Service Cancellation
detections.description: Phone, internet, insurance, or utilities cancelled without knowledge or consent.

detections.name: Unauthorised Service Changes
detections.description: Service plans modified or features removed without notification.

techniques.name: Location-Based Assault
techniques.description: Using GPS tracking, location sharing, or other surveillance techniques to determine victim's real-time location and then physically approaching or assaulting them. Technology enables perpetrator to find victim at any location, negating traditional safety measures like staying with friends or varying routines.
techniques.public_title: Using Your Location to Find and Harm You
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses tracking technology to locate you and then physically approaches, confronts, or assaults you. Technology enables the physical harm by revealing where you are.
techniques.safety_warning: If you are in immediate danger, call 000. If you suspect someone is tracking your location to find you, contact police and a support service for safety planning.

notices.signal: The other person shows up at places you haven't told them about
notices.detail: They appear at locations that should be unknown to them.

notices.signal: Confrontations happen at locations you only visited once
notices.detail: They're tracking your movements in real time.

actions.action: Review all tracking and location sharing immediately
actions.detail: Check your phone, car, and belongings for trackers. Review all app permissions.

actions.action: Create a safety plan with a support service
actions.detail: 1800RESPECT and local DV services can help you plan for physical safety.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Location-based stalking and assault are serious crimes.

mitigations.name: Comprehensive Location Security
mitigations.description: Disable all location sharing, remove trackers, secure location-revealing accounts, vary routines.

mitigations.name: Safety Planning
mitigations.description: Develop comprehensive safety plan with support service addressing technology-enabled tracking.

mitigations.name: Law Enforcement Report
mitigations.description: Report stalking and tracking to police. Apply for intervention order with technology-specific conditions.

detections.name: Location Interception
detections.description: Adversary appears at locations not disclosed to them.

detections.name: Location-Referencing Threats
detections.description: Threats that reference specific location or recent movements.

techniques.name: Safe Location Disclosure
techniques.description: Revealing the location of victim's shelter, safe house, refuge, or hidden address to the perpetrator or others. May involve sharing information publicly, telling mutual contacts, or using technology to discover and disclose the protected location, directly endangering victim's physical safety.
techniques.public_summary: Someone discovers and reveals the address of your refuge, shelter, safe house, or new home — putting you and potentially others at risk.
techniques.safety_warning: If your safe location has been compromised, contact the service managing your safety immediately. You may need to relocate.

notices.signal: The other person references or appears near your safe location
notices.detail: They know where you're staying despite it being confidential.

notices.signal: You receive communications indicating your address is known
notices.detail: Messages referencing your current location.

actions.action: Contact your support service or refuge immediately
actions.detail: They can help assess the risk and arrange relocation if needed.

actions.action: Contact police if there's an immediate safety threat
actions.detail: Call 000 if you're in danger.

actions.action: Review how the location may have been discovered
actions.detail: Check devices for tracking, review social media for location clues, and consider whether anyone might have shared the information.

mitigations.name: Safe Location Digital Hygiene
mitigations.description: Disable location services. Strip metadata from images. Avoid tagging safe location digitally.

mitigations.name: Secure Communication from Safe Location
mitigations.description: Use new device and accounts. Only communicate location to those who must know via secure channels.

detections.name: Safe Location Discovery
detections.description: Adversary appears near or references safe location. Immediate safety emergency.

detections.name: Photo Metadata Exposure
detections.description: Shared photos contain GPS coordinates revealing safe location.

techniques.name: Movement Interception
techniques.description: Using location tracking data to intercept victim during travel, at appointments, or at known destinations. Perpetrator uses real-time or predicted location information to position themselves along victim's route or at their destination. Creates a sense of inescapable surveillance and control.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses technology to predict or track your travel routes and intercepts you — appearing on your commute, following your car, or confronting you during transit.
techniques.safety_warning: If someone is intercepting your movements, vary your routes and times. Contact police.

notices.signal: The other person appears on your commute or regular routes
notices.detail: They show up along paths they shouldn't know about.

notices.signal: Your travel patterns seem to be predicted
notices.detail: They know when you leave and which route you take.

actions.action: Vary your routes and times
actions.detail: Don't follow the same pattern every day.

actions.action: Check your vehicle for GPS trackers
actions.detail: Inspect thoroughly, including underneath.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: This constitutes stalking.

mitigations.name: Route Variation
mitigations.description: Vary routes, departure times, and transport methods.

mitigations.name: Appointment Security
mitigations.description: Keep appointments off monitored calendars. Arrange support person accompaniment.

detections.name: Route Interception
detections.description: Adversary appearing along travel route or at destinations.

detections.name: Travel Knowledge Indicators
detections.description: Adversary demonstrates knowledge of travel plans before arrival.

techniques.name: Smart Lock Manipulation
techniques.description: Remotely locking victim inside or outside of their residence, changing access codes, or manipulating smart lock systems to control victim's physical movement and access to shelter. May also include granting access to others or monitoring entry/exit patterns.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses smart lock access to lock you in or out of your home, change access codes, or create an unsafe environment — especially after separation when they retain admin access.
techniques.safety_warning: If you are locked in your home and feel unsafe, call 000.

notices.signal: Smart lock codes stop working or change without your input
notices.detail: You can't get in or out of your home.

notices.signal: The other person lets themselves in after you've changed physical locks
notices.detail: They still have smart lock access.

notices.signal: Lock activity logs show access at times the other person shouldn't be entering
notices.detail: The smart lock records show unauthorised entries.

actions.action: Factory reset smart locks and set up new codes
actions.detail: Remove all previous users and start fresh.

actions.action: Consider replacing smart locks with traditional deadbolts
actions.detail: Physical locks can't be controlled remotely.

actions.action: Contact a locksmith who understands smart home security
actions.detail: They can ensure your home is properly secured.

mitigations.name: Smart Lock Security Reset
mitigations.description: Change all smart lock credentials. Remove adversary access. Replace with traditional locks if needed.

mitigations.name: Lock Replacement Post-Separation
mitigations.description: Change all locks after separation. Most jurisdictions require landlords to do this for DFV situations.

detections.name: Lock Behaviour Anomalies
detections.description: Smart locks engaging or disengaging unexpectedly. Access codes no longer working.

detections.name: Physical Access Control
detections.description: Locked inside or outside home due to remote lock manipulation. Safety emergency.

techniques.name: Vehicle Sabotage
techniques.description: Remotely disabling, manipulating, or monitoring victim's connected vehicle. Modern connected cars may be remotely controlled through manufacturer apps, including locking/unlocking, starting/stopping engine, tracking location, and in some cases controlling speed or braking. May also include disabling vehicle through telematics systems.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses technology to interfere with your vehicle — disabling features through connected car apps, tracking via built-in GPS, or sabotaging vehicle systems.
techniques.safety_warning: Vehicle sabotage is dangerous. If you suspect interference with your car, have it inspected by a mechanic before driving.

notices.signal: Vehicle features stop working or behave strangely
notices.detail: Remote start, locking, or other connected features malfunction.

notices.signal: The other person uses a connected car app to track or control your vehicle
notices.detail: They can see your location or disable features through the manufacturer's app.

actions.action: Contact the vehicle manufacturer about removing the other person's app access
actions.detail: Explain the situation and request sole account control.

actions.action: Have the vehicle inspected by a mechanic
actions.detail: Check for trackers and tampering.

actions.action: Change the connected car account passwords
actions.detail: Remove the other person's access to vehicle apps.

mitigations.name: Connected Car Account Security
mitigations.description: Change connected car credentials. Remove adversary from vehicle account access.

mitigations.name: Vehicle Safety Inspection
mitigations.description: Have mechanic inspect for tracking devices and tampering. Check OBD-II port.

detections.name: Remote Vehicle Control
detections.description: Vehicle functions activating without user action — horn, lights, locks, engine.

detections.name: Connected Car Access Alerts
detections.description: Notifications showing adversary's device accessing vehicle features.

sub_techniques.name: Connected Vehicle Remote Control
sub_techniques.description: Using manufacturer apps (Tesla, BMW Connected, MySubaru, FordPass) to remotely lock/unlock, start/stop engine, honk horn, flash lights, adjust climate, or disable a connected vehicle. Modern connected cars provide extensive remote control capabilities through smartphone apps, and the person who set up the app retains control even after separation.
sub_techniques.public_title: Someone is remotely controlling your car through an app
sub_techniques.public_summary: Modern cars can be controlled through smartphone apps — locking doors, starting the engine, honking the horn, or even disabling the vehicle. If your ex-partner set up the car's app account, they may still have control.

notices.signal: Your car does things by itself — horn honking, lights flashing, doors locking
notices.detail: These can all be triggered remotely through the manufacturer's app.

notices.signal: Your car won't start or suddenly shuts off
notices.detail: Some connected car apps allow remote engine disable.

actions.action: Contact the car manufacturer to transfer the connected account
actions.detail: The dealership or manufacturer can remove the previous owner's access and set up a new account for you.

actions.action: Change the car's PIN/password if applicable
actions.detail: Some vehicles have their own PIN codes independent of the app.

techniques.name: IoT Device Weaponization
techniques.description: Using smart home devices to create fear, disorientation, or physical discomfort. Includes randomly triggering alarms, playing sounds through speakers, turning lights on/off, changing temperature extremes, activating cameras, or other manipulations of the smart home environment designed to terrorize victim.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses internet-connected devices to create fear, discomfort, or danger — playing sounds at night, extreme temperature changes, turning off security systems, or other disruptive actions.
techniques.safety_warning: If IoT devices are creating unsafe conditions, disconnect them. Your safety is more important than smart home convenience.

notices.signal: Devices activate at disturbing times
notices.detail: Speakers play sounds at night, lights flash, or alarms trigger.

notices.signal: Heating or cooling goes to extremes
notices.detail: Temperature is set dangerously high or low.

notices.signal: Security cameras or systems are disabled
notices.detail: Your security devices stop working.

actions.action: Unplug or disconnect concerning devices
actions.detail: Remove the immediate threat.

actions.action: Change your Wi-Fi password
actions.detail: This disconnects all smart devices.

actions.action: Factory reset and reconfigure only essential devices
actions.detail: Set them up on accounts only you control.

mitigations.name: IoT Device Audit and Reset
mitigations.description: Audit all smart home devices. Factory reset and reconfigure under sole-controlled account.

mitigations.name: Network Security
mitigations.description: Change Wi-Fi passwords. Remove adversary access to router admin.

detections.name: Unexplained Device Activation
detections.description: Smart home devices activating without user command — alarms, lights, speakers, TV.

detections.name: Environmental Manipulation
detections.description: Temperature or comfort settings changed remotely to create discomfort.

techniques.name: Medical Device Interference
techniques.description: Tampering with victim's connected medical devices, health monitoring equipment, or health data. May include altering medication reminder settings, manipulating health data to affect treatment decisions, disabling monitoring devices, or interfering with telehealth appointments. Creates direct physical health risks.
techniques.public_summary: Someone interferes with technology-connected medical devices or health management systems — insulin pumps, medication reminders, CPAP machines, or other health-critical technology.
techniques.safety_warning: Interference with medical devices can be life-threatening. Contact your healthcare provider and police immediately.

notices.signal: Medical device settings have been changed
notices.detail: Dosages, schedules, or configurations are different from what was prescribed.

notices.signal: Medication reminders or health apps have been altered
notices.detail: Alarms are turned off, medications are removed from tracking apps, or prescriptions are cancelled.

actions.action: Contact your healthcare provider immediately
actions.detail: Report the interference and get your medical devices checked.

actions.action: Secure access to medical device apps and accounts
actions.detail: Change passwords and remove the other person's access.

actions.action: Report to police
actions.detail: Interfering with medical devices is a serious criminal offence.

mitigations.name: Medical Device Security Review
mitigations.description: Inform healthcare provider of DFV situation. Request security review of connected medical devices.

mitigations.name: Health Record Access Control
mitigations.description: Restrict health record access. Change patient portal credentials. Remove adversary as authorised contact.

detections.name: Medical Device Setting Changes
detections.description: Connected medical device settings changed without user action. Contact healthcare provider immediately.

detections.name: Health Data Access Indicators
detections.description: Adversary demonstrates knowledge of health information they should not have access to.

techniques.name: Stalking Coordination
techniques.description: Using technology to plan, coordinate, and execute physical stalking of victim. Includes using location data to track patterns, mapping victim's routine, coordinating with others to maintain surveillance, and using digital tools to avoid detection. Technology amplifies traditional stalking by providing real-time intelligence.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses multiple technology methods together to stalk you — combining phone tracking, social media monitoring, third-party informants, and physical surveillance into a persistent pattern.
techniques.safety_warning: Coordinated stalking is dangerous and often escalates. Contact police and a specialist stalking support service.

notices.signal: The other person knows your movements with impossible precision

techniques.public_summary: Someone makes false reports to police, child protection, or other authorities about you — sending emergency services to your home, triggering investigations, or creating a record of false complaints.
techniques.safety_warning: If authorities arrive based on false reports, stay calm and cooperate. Document the false report for your own records and tell your lawyer.

notices.signal: A pattern of false reports emerges

actions.action: Report false emergency calls as criminal offences

actions.action: Keep a chronological record of all false reports

Exploits legitimate co-parenting technology to maintain perpetrator's access to and control over victim's life through the children.
techniques.public_summary: Someone uses custody arrangements as a channel for technology-facilitated abuse — monitoring through children's devices, using co-parenting apps for harassment, or leveraging custody exchanges for surveillance.
techniques.safety_warning: Children's safety is paramount. Document all technology misuse through custody arrangements for family court.

notices.signal: Co-parenting apps are used for hostile messages instead of co-parenting
notices.detail: The communication platform becomes a harassment tool.

notices.signal: Children's devices have monitoring software that enables household surveillance

actions.action: Use court-approved co-parenting apps

actions.action: Check children's devices for monitoring software
actions.detail: Audit apps and permissions on devices the children bring between homes.

actions.action: Document all technology misuse for family court

techniques.name: Online Target Identification
techniques.description: Using social media, dating platforms, forums, or gaming platforms to identify and select potential victims based on vulnerability indicators such as loneliness, recent breakup, financial difficulty, age, or naivety. The perpetrator scouts for targets before making contact, often reviewing profiles, post history, and public information to assess susceptibility.
techniques.public_title: Someone may be watching your online activity to target you
techniques.public_summary: Before making contact, some people carefully study social media profiles, dating app activity, or online posts to find someone they think they can manipulate. They look for signs of loneliness, recent heartbreak, financial stress, or trusting nature.

notices.signal: A stranger seems to know a lot about you from the start
notices.detail: They reference things from your profile, posts, or comments in a way that feels like they've done research.

notices.signal: Someone contacts you right after you've posted about something difficult
notices.detail: Predators and scammers monitor for vulnerability signals like breakup posts, grief, or financial stress.

notices.signal: The approach feels perfectly tailored to you
notices.detail: They share your exact interests, values, or experiences — it feels like destiny but may be calculated.

actions.action: Review what's public on your profiles
actions.detail: Check what strangers can see on your social media, dating profiles, and forum accounts. Consider limiting what's visible.

actions.action: Be cautious with new contacts who seem to know you well
actions.detail: If someone you've just met seems unusually attuned to your situation, that may be strategic rather than genuine connection.

actions.action: Talk to your children about online stranger contact
actions.detail: Help young people understand that adults who contact them online may have studied their profiles first.
actions.safety_note: Frame this as awareness, not fear — the goal is informed caution.

sub_techniques.name: Dating Platform Target Selection
sub_techniques.description: Using dating apps (Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, Grindr) to identify targets, often filtering for vulnerability signals in profiles such as recently single status, mentions of loneliness, or indicators of financial situation.
sub_techniques.public_summary: Someone uses dating apps to find people they can exploit — looking for signs of vulnerability in profiles and conversations.

notices.signal: They move very fast emotionally
notices.detail: Intense declarations of feelings within days. This pace is designed to overwhelm your judgement.

notices.signal: They want to move off the dating app quickly
notices.detail: Pushing to WhatsApp, Telegram, or phone calls before you're comfortable removes the platform's safety features.

actions.action: Keep conversations on the platform initially
actions.detail: Dating apps have reporting and blocking features. Moving to private messaging removes those protections.

actions.action: Do a reverse image search on their photos
actions.detail: Scammers often use stolen photos. A reverse image search can reveal if the photos belong to someone else.

sub_techniques.name: Gaming Platform Target Selection
sub_techniques.description: Identifying targets (often minors) via gaming platforms (Roblox, Minecraft, Fortnite, Discord) based on age indicators, activity patterns, in-game behaviour, and willingness to engage in chat. Groomers look for children who seem isolated, eager for attention, or responsive to gifts.
sub_techniques.public_summary: Adults use gaming platforms to find children they can build relationships with. They look for kids who seem lonely, who respond to attention, or who accept in-game gifts.

notices.signal: An older player is giving your child lots of attention
notices.detail: Buying them in-game items, always wanting to play together, asking personal questions.

notices.signal: Your child has a new 'best friend' online they won't talk about
notices.detail: Secrecy about online friendships is a warning sign, especially with age gaps.

notices.signal: Your child is receiving gifts (game currency, items, subscriptions)
notices.detail: Gift-giving creates obligation and is a classic grooming technique.

actions.action: Know what games your child plays and who they play with
actions.detail: You don't need to monitor every message, but understanding who they interact with regularly matters.
actions.safety_note: Frame this as interest in their world, not surveillance.

actions.action: Set up parental controls on gaming platforms
actions.detail: Most platforms have settings to limit who can contact your child or send friend requests.

actions.action: Report to ACCCE if you're concerned about an adult contacting your child
actions.detail: The Australian Centre to Counter Child Exploitation: accce.gov.au/report

sub_techniques.name: Social Media Target Selection
sub_techniques.description: Identifying targets via Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, Facebook based on public posts, follower counts, content themes, geographic indicators, or visible vulnerability. Both child and adult targeting occurs through social media.
sub_techniques.public_summary: Someone studies your social media activity to decide whether and how to approach you. Public posts, check-ins, relationship status, and even the tone of your captions can be used to assess vulnerability.

notices.signal: A stranger follows you and immediately starts engaging with all your content
notices.detail: Liking old posts, commenting on everything, sharing your stories — creating a sense of connection quickly.

notices.signal: They seem to share all your interests and values
notices.detail: This mirroring is a common manipulation technique — they've read your profile and are reflecting it back.

actions.action: Set your accounts to private
actions.detail: Limit who can see your posts, stories, and personal information.

actions.action: Be cautious about what you share publicly
actions.detail: Location check-ins, relationship updates, and emotional posts can all be used to assess your vulnerability.

techniques.name: Trust Building & Love Bombing
techniques.description: Overwhelming the target with attention, affection, compliments, gifts, or constant communication to create emotional dependency and false intimacy. In romance fraud, this is the 'fattening' phase. In child grooming, this is the befriending stage. The perpetrator mirrors the target's interests, validates their feelings, and positions themselves as uniquely understanding and trustworthy.
techniques.public_title: Someone is overwhelming you with attention and affection
techniques.public_summary: They message constantly, shower you with compliments, say you're 'the only one who understands them,' and make you feel like the centre of their world. This intensity feels amazing — but healthy relationships don't start at full speed.

notices.signal: The relationship is moving incredibly fast
notices.detail: Declarations of love within days or weeks. Talking about a future together before you've really gotten to know each other.

notices.signal: They're available all the time
notices.detail: Instant responses to every message, always wanting to talk, checking in constantly. It feels attentive but it's creating dependency.

notices.signal: They mirror everything about you
notices.detail: They love the same music, share the same values, have the same dreams. It feels like soulmates but may be calculated reflection.

notices.signal: They share 'deep secrets' to create false intimacy
notices.detail: Telling you vulnerable things about themselves early on to encourage you to do the same. This creates a sense of mutual trust that hasn't been earned.

notices.signal: You feel guilty when you're not available to them
notices.detail: If you don't respond quickly or need space, they make you feel like you've hurt them. This is the obligation forming.

actions.action: Slow down
actions.detail: A genuine connection will still be there next week, next month. If someone can't handle you taking things at a comfortable pace, that tells you something.

actions.action: Maintain your other relationships
actions.detail: If you're spending less time with friends and family because of this new person, notice that shift.

actions.action: Ask yourself: would I accept this pace from anyone else?
actions.detail: Remove the feelings for a moment and look at the behaviour pattern. Is this how healthy relationships normally start?

actions.action: Talk to someone you trust about the relationship
actions.detail: Describe what's happening to a friend, family member, or counsellor. Outside perspective can see patterns you're too close to notice.
actions.safety_note: Use a safe device if you think your communications might be monitored.

sub_techniques.name: Gift & Financial Grooming
sub_techniques.description: Sending gifts, game currency, gift cards, small amounts of money, or paying for things to build obligation and emotional debt. In gaming contexts, buying in-game items for minors. In romance fraud, sending flowers or small transfers. Creates reciprocity pressure — the target feels they 'owe' something in return.
sub_techniques.public_title: Someone is giving you gifts to create obligation
sub_techniques.public_summary: They buy you things, send money, pay for meals, or give your child in-game items. This feels generous but it creates a feeling of owing them — which they will eventually use.

notices.signal: The gifts come before you've established a real relationship
notices.detail: Generosity from someone you barely know is a warning sign, not a green flag.

notices.signal: You feel uncomfortable saying no to their requests because of what they've given you
notices.detail: This is the obligation working exactly as intended.

actions.action: You don't owe anyone anything because they gave you something
actions.detail: A genuine gift has no strings attached. If you feel pressure to reciprocate, that's a signal.

actions.action: Tell your children: adults shouldn't be buying them things online
actions.detail: Especially from people they don't know in person.

techniques.name: Boundary Testing & Desensitisation
techniques.description: Making incrementally escalating requests to test compliance and normalise boundary violations. Starts small (share your location, send a photo, stay up late talking) and escalates (send intimate content, meet in person, transfer money, cut off contact with friends). The request-demand-threaten-force escalation sequence. Each compliance makes the next request harder to refuse.
techniques.public_title: Someone is pushing your boundaries and it keeps getting worse
techniques.public_summary: It started with small requests — share your location, let me see your phone, send a photo. Over time the requests got bigger, more personal, more uncomfortable. When you say no, they react badly. This pattern of testing what they can get you to do is not normal relationship behaviour.

notices.signal: Requests start small and gradually get bigger
notices.detail: They might start by asking you to share your location 'so they know you're safe,' then escalate to wanting access to your messages, then your passwords.

notices.signal: They guilt-trip you when you say no
notices.detail: 'If you loved me you would...' or 'I thought you trusted me.' Making you feel bad for having boundaries.

notices.signal: They frame boundary violations as proof of love
notices.detail: 'I only check your phone because I care.' Normal relationships don't require giving up your privacy.

notices.signal: You feel like you 'owe' them something
notices.detail: Especially after they've given you gifts, attention, or support — this creates a sense of obligation that they exploit.

notices.signal: Things that felt uncomfortable now feel normal
notices.detail: You've gradually adjusted to behaviour that would have alarmed you at the start. This is desensitisation — and it's deliberate.

actions.action: Trust your discomfort
actions.detail: If something feels wrong, it probably is. You don't need to justify saying no.

actions.action: Talk to someone you trust
actions.detail: A friend, family member, counsellor, or helpline. Describe the pattern, not just individual incidents.
actions.safety_note: Use a safe device if you think your communications are monitored.

actions.action: Know that this is a pattern, not a one-off
actions.detail: If requests keep escalating and 'no' is never accepted, this is a control pattern. It's not about this one request — it's about establishing that your boundaries don't matter.

techniques.name: Isolation from Protective Networks
techniques.description: Encouraging or engineering the target's separation from friends, family, or online communities who might recognise the grooming pattern. 'They don't understand us.' 'Your parents wouldn't get it.' 'Your friends are jealous.' Undermines existing relationships to increase dependency on the perpetrator.
techniques.public_title: Someone is trying to separate you from the people who care about you
techniques.public_summary: They suggest your friends don't really understand you, your family is too controlling, or that other people are jealous of your relationship. Gradually, they become the only person you feel you can talk to. This isn't love — it's isolation.

notices.signal: They criticise your friends and family
notices.detail: Subtle at first — 'I just think they don't appreciate you' — then more directly undermining your relationships.

notices.signal: They want to be your only source of support
notices.detail: 'You don't need them, you have me.' Creating a world where they're the centre.

notices.signal: You're spending less time with people who matter to you
notices.detail: If your social world has shrunk since this relationship started, notice that.

notices.signal: They react badly when you make plans without them
notices.detail: Guilt, anger, sulking, or accusations when you spend time with others.

actions.action: Maintain your existing relationships
actions.detail: Keep seeing friends and family, even if the other person doesn't like it. The people who were there before this relationship are your safety net.

actions.action: Notice if your world is getting smaller
actions.detail: A healthy relationship adds to your life — it doesn't replace everything else in it.

actions.action: Tell someone what's happening
actions.detail: If you feel like you can't talk to anyone about this relationship, that itself is a warning sign.
actions.safety_note: Use a safe device to reach out if needed.

techniques.name: Migration to Private/Encrypted Platforms
techniques.description: Moving communication from public or monitored platforms to private, encrypted, or ephemeral channels (Telegram, Signal, Snapchat, WhatsApp) to avoid detection by parents, platform moderation, or law enforcement. Framed as 'more personal' or 'more private' but the purpose is removing safety infrastructure.
techniques.public_title: They want to move your conversations somewhere more 'private'
techniques.public_summary: They suggest moving from a dating app, gaming platform, or social media to a private messaging app — 'so we can talk properly.' This removes the safety features of the original platform and makes the conversation harder for anyone else to see.

notices.signal: They push to move off the original platform early
notices.detail: Before you've really gotten to know them, they want to switch to WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, or phone calls.

notices.signal: They specifically want ephemeral messaging
notices.detail: Snapchat (messages disappear), Telegram (secret chats), Signal (disappearing messages) — they want conversations that don't leave a trail.

notices.signal: They frame it as romantic or special
notices.detail: 'I want to talk to you properly, not on here.' It sounds sweet but it removes your safety net.

actions.action: Keep conversations on the original platform until you're comfortable
actions.detail: Dating apps, gaming platforms, and social media have reporting and blocking features. Private messaging doesn't.

actions.action: Ask yourself why they need to move platforms
actions.detail: If someone is genuine, they'll be happy to keep talking wherever you're comfortable.

actions.action: Tell your children: if an online friend wants to move to a different app, tell an adult
actions.detail: This is one of the clearest warning signs in child grooming.

sub_techniques.name: Snapchat Exploitation
sub_techniques.description: Using Snapchat's disappearing messages and Snap Map features specifically because content auto-deletes, reducing evidence. Quick Add and Snap Map enable contact with minors based on location proximity. The ephemeral nature of Snapchat makes it the platform of choice for grooming conversations that the perpetrator doesn't want recorded.
sub_techniques.public_summary: Snapchat messages disappear after viewing, which means there's less evidence. Someone may specifically choose Snapchat for conversations they don't want anyone else to see.

notices.signal: They only want to talk on Snapchat, not other platforms
notices.detail: If someone insists on Snapchat specifically, consider why they want disappearing messages.

notices.signal: Your child has Snapstreaks with people they don't know in person
notices.detail: Maintaining daily Snap streaks creates a sense of obligation and routine contact.

actions.action: Disable Snap Map or set to Ghost Mode
actions.detail: Snap Map shows your real-time location to friends. Ghost Mode hides your location from everyone.

actions.action: Parents: review your child's Snapchat friend list
actions.detail: Look for contacts they don't know in person, especially adults.
actions.safety_note: Have the conversation about why, not just what you're checking.

techniques.name: Age/Identity Deception
techniques.description: Misrepresenting age, identity, appearance, occupation, or circumstances to build trust. Includes catfishing, using stolen photos, creating false personas, and age misrepresentation by adults targeting minors or by scammers targeting adults. The deception is the foundation on which the exploitative relationship is built.
techniques.public_title: The person you're talking to may not be who they say they are
techniques.public_summary: They might be using someone else's photos, lying about their age, inventing a life story, or pretending to be someone they're not. Online, identity is easy to fake — and some people build entire false personas to exploit others.

notices.signal: They won't video call or always have an excuse
notices.detail: If someone avoids showing their face live, they may not look like their photos.

notices.signal: Their story has inconsistencies
notices.detail: Details about their life, job, location, or past don't add up or change over time.

notices.signal: A reverse image search shows their photos belong to someone else
notices.detail: This is a strong indicator of catfishing or scam activity.

notices.signal: They claim to be younger/older than they appear
notices.detail: Especially concerning when an adult claims to be a teenager to contact minors.

actions.action: Do a reverse image search
actions.detail: Right-click their profile photo and search Google Images, or use TinEye. If the photo appears elsewhere with a different name, it's likely stolen.

actions.action: Video call before meeting in person
actions.detail: A genuine person will be happy to video call. Persistent refusal is a red flag.

actions.action: Talk to children about online identity deception
actions.detail: Help young people understand that the person they're talking to online may not be who they claim.
actions.safety_note: Frame this as 'people online can pretend to be anyone' rather than creating fear.

techniques.description: Using livestreaming platforms (Twitch, YouTube Live, TikTok Live, Instagram Live) to make initial contact with minors, build relationships through donations/gifts, engage in chat, and move to private communication. techniques.public_summary: Adults watch children's livestreams and use the chat, donations, or direct messages to build a relationship. The attention and gifts feel exciting — but an adult consistently engaging with a child's livestream is a warning sign.

notices.signal: Your child is receiving donations or gifts from adult viewers
notices.detail: Money or virtual gifts from strangers during livestreams create obligation.

notices.signal: An adult viewer is consistently present and commenting
notices.detail: Regular engagement from an adult in a child's chat is concerning.

notices.signal: The viewer moves to direct messaging
notices.detail: Moving from public chat to private DMs is a key escalation step.

notices.signal: Your child is livestreaming to strangers
notices.detail: Children may not understand that livestreaming is broadcasting to an unknown audience.

actions.action: Talk to your child about who watches their streams
actions.detail: Help them understand that their audience includes strangers, and that adult attention isn't always positive.

actions.action: Set livestreaming accounts to friends-only or disable
actions.detail: Most platforms allow restricting who can view streams and comment.

actions.action: Report concerning adults to the platform and ACCCE
actions.detail: accce.gov.au/report for child exploitation concerns.

techniques.name: AI-Assisted Grooming
techniques.description: Using AI chatbots, LLMs, or automated messaging to maintain multiple grooming relationships simultaneously at scale. AI enables personalised, varied manipulation conversations that adapt to each target's responses. The 'pig butchering' industrial model uses AI to manage hundreds of simultaneous relationships, with human operators stepping in for high-value interactions.
techniques.public_title: The person you're talking to might be a chatbot — or managed by AI
techniques.public_summary: Scam operations now use AI to have convincing conversations with many people at once. The messages feel personal and genuine, but they're generated by software designed to build trust and extract money or compliance.

notices.signal: Responses come at unusual hours with no delay
notices.detail: AI doesn't sleep. If someone always responds instantly, regardless of time zone, that's worth noticing.

notices.signal: Their writing style is very consistent and polished
notices.detail: Real humans have typos, moods, and variations. AI-generated messages can be unnaturally consistent.

notices.signal: They never make mistakes or reference real-world spontaneous events
notices.detail: AI conversations can feel perfect but lack the messiness of real life.

notices.signal: They deflect or change subject when you ask specific questions
notices.detail: AI-managed conversations struggle with unexpected, specific, or off-script questions.

actions.action: Ask unexpected, specific questions
actions.detail: What's the weather like where you are right now? What did you have for breakfast? Real people answer easily. AI-managed conversations stumble.

actions.action: Insist on a live video call
actions.detail: This is the single most effective way to verify you're talking to a real person. If they won't or can't, be very cautious.

actions.action: If they ask for money, it's almost certainly a scam
actions.detail: No matter how real the relationship feels, if money is requested — it's the extraction phase.

techniques.name: Sextortion-as-Grooming
techniques.description: The pattern where initial sextortion of a minor transitions into ongoing control and exploitation. The first coerced image becomes permanent leverage for escalating demands — more images, sexual acts, money, or compliance. The perpetrator uses shame and fear of parental discovery as ongoing leverage. This is the intersection of grooming and sextortion responsible for a significant number of teen male suicides.
techniques.public_title: Someone is using intimate images to control you or your child
techniques.public_summary: They convinced you (or your child) to share an intimate image, and now they're using it as leverage — demanding more images, money, or compliance. The threat of exposure feels overwhelming, but compliance almost always leads to escalation, not safety.
techniques.safety_warning: If you or your child is experiencing this: do not comply with further demands. Compliance almost never stops the demands — it escalates them. This is not your fault, regardless of what was shared. Help is available and this can be stopped.

notices.signal: Demands escalate after the first image is shared
notices.detail: What started as one image becomes demands for more, for video, for money, for meeting in person.

notices.signal: Threats to send images to friends, family, or school
notices.detail: The perpetrator uses the victim's social network as leverage — 'I'll send this to everyone you know.'

notices.signal: Your child suddenly becomes withdrawn, anxious, or changes device behaviour
notices.detail: Secrecy about their phone, staying up late, emotional distress — these can indicate sextortion.

notices.signal: Unexplained money transfers from your child's accounts
notices.detail: Some sextortion demands are financial — the child may be sending money to make it stop.

actions.action: Stop all communication with the person making demands
actions.detail: Block them on every platform. Do not respond to threats. They are counting on your fear.
actions.safety_note: If you're concerned about immediate safety, contact police.

actions.action: Do not pay or send more content
actions.detail: Paying or complying does not make it stop. It proves the leverage works and demands will escalate.

actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner
actions.detail: The eSafety Commissioner can issue takedown notices to platforms and help with image removal. esafety.gov.au

actions.action: Talk to your child with compassion, not anger
actions.detail: They are the victim. Their biggest fear is your reaction. Respond with support and they'll let you help.
actions.safety_note: What they need to hear: 'This is not your fault. I'm not angry. We will sort this out together.'

actions.action: Report to police and ACCCE for child victims
actions.detail: This is a crime. accce.gov.au/report for child exploitation. Police for all victims.

techniques.public_summary: Some online communities and influencers teach that monitoring your partner, controlling their behaviour, and using manipulation are normal parts of relationships. This content radicalises people — often young men — into believing abuse is acceptable.

notices.signal: Someone in your life starts using language about 'high value' people or 'alpha' behaviour
notices.detail: This language often comes from communities that normalise control and dehumanise partners.

notices.signal: They talk about relationships in transactional terms
notices.detail: Viewing relationships as exchanges of value rather than partnerships of equals is a red flag.

notices.signal: They justify monitoring or controlling behaviour as 'protecting' the relationship
notices.detail: Framing surveillance as care is a learned pattern from these communities.

actions.action: Recognise the pattern

actions.action: Talk to young people about what they're watching
actions.detail: Many teenagers encounter this content through algorithm recommendations on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram.
actions.safety_note: Approach with curiosity, not judgement — 'what are you watching?' not 'that's terrible.'

techniques.description: Being recruited into organised fraud/scam operations (often through false job advertisements) and trained in romance fraud, sextortion, and social engineering techniques at scale. Recruited individuals are often themselves trafficked and exploited. The 'Nigerian Prince' industrial pipeline — from recruitment to training to operation. techniques.public_title: Organised scam operations train people to exploit you
techniques.public_summary: The romance scam or sextortion you're experiencing may be run by an organised operation that recruits, trains, and manages dozens of scammers. The person messaging you may themselves be a victim of trafficking, following a script provided by criminal operators.

notices.signal: The scam feels professional and well-rehearsed
notices.detail: Multiple stages, consistent messaging, coordinated pressure — this is an operation, not one person.

notices.signal: They shift from emotional to financial requests in a predictable pattern
notices.detail: The 'pig butchering' model follows a documented sequence: build trust → introduce investment opportunity → extract funds.

actions.action: Report to ReportCyber (cyber.gov.au)
actions.detail: Australian Cyber Security Centre's reporting mechanism for cybercrime.

actions.action: Report to your bank immediately if money has been sent
actions.detail: Some transactions can be reversed if reported quickly.

actions.action: Don't blame yourself
actions.detail: These operations are designed by professionals specifically to exploit human trust. Being targeted is not a reflection of your intelligence.

techniques.name: Child Device Monitoring Abuse
techniques.description: Using parental monitoring on children's devices to surveil an ex-partner's activities, location, and communications through the child. The child's device becomes a surveillance tool against the other parent. Distinct from Child Custody Tech Abuse (SAFE-T-0145) where the child is the target — here the child is the vector.
techniques.public_title: Someone may be using your child's devices to monitor you
techniques.public_summary: Your ex-partner may have installed monitoring software or configured parental controls on your children's devices — not to protect the children, but to track your location, read your messages through the child, or monitor what happens in your home.
techniques.safety_warning: Be careful about discussing sensitive matters near your children's devices if you suspect monitoring. Consider whether devices given to children by the other parent may have monitoring enabled.

notices.signal: Your ex seems to know details about your home life they shouldn't know
notices.detail: Conversations, visitors, your schedule — information that could only come from inside your home.

notices.signal: The children's devices have parental monitoring you didn't set up
notices.detail: Check for apps like Life360, Find My, or other tracking/monitoring apps on devices provided by the other parent.

notices.signal: Your ex references your location when the children are with you
notices.detail: If they know where you went while the children had their devices, the devices may be tracking.

actions.action: Check children's devices for monitoring apps
actions.detail: Look for parental control apps, location sharing, and device administrator settings you didn't configure.
actions.safety_note: If you find monitoring, get advice before removing it — the other parent may be alerted.

actions.action: Consider a separate device for sensitive communication
actions.detail: Keep important calls and messages off any device the children carry between homes.

actions.action: Document and seek legal advice
actions.detail: Using children's devices for surveillance may violate family court orders and surveillance legislation.

techniques.public_title: Someone may be using AI to create fake evidence against you
techniques.public_summary: AI can now generate convincing fake text message screenshots, emails, documents, and even audio recordings. Someone may use these fakes in court, with your employer, with child protection, or to damage your reputation.

notices.signal: Evidence is presented that shows conversations you never had
notices.detail: Screenshots of messages you didn't send, emails you didn't write, documents you didn't create.

notices.signal: The evidence seems too perfect
notices.detail: Real conversations are messy. Fabricated ones can be unnaturally clean, perfectly supporting the other person's narrative.

notices.signal: Metadata doesn't match
notices.detail: A forensic examiner can check whether screenshots, documents, or recordings have been generated or manipulated.

actions.action: Preserve your own records
actions.detail: Keep your actual message history, emails, and documents. Your real records are the best defence against fabricated ones.

actions.action: Request forensic analysis of suspicious evidence
actions.detail: AI-generated content often has detectable artefacts. A digital forensic expert can identify fabrication.

actions.action: Alert your lawyer to the possibility of AI fabrication
actions.detail: Courts are increasingly aware of this issue but your legal team needs to know to challenge suspect evidence.

techniques.name: Weaponised Welfare Checks
techniques.description: Repeatedly calling police or child protection services to conduct welfare checks on the victim, using state agencies as a harassment tool. Reports are technically 'concerned' but the pattern is punitive — using volume and frequency to exhaust, intimidate, and signal that the perpetrator can deploy the state against the victim at any time. Distinct from Swatting (immediate physical danger) and Emergency Service Manipulation (false reports for legal advantage).
techniques.public_title: Someone is sending police or child protection to your door repeatedly
techniques.public_summary: Your ex-partner or someone else is making repeated reports to police, child protection, or other agencies to trigger welfare checks at your home. Each individual report may seem 'concerned,' but the pattern is harassment — designed to exhaust you, intimidate you, and signal that they can bring the state to your door whenever they want.

notices.signal: Police or child protection visit you repeatedly based on reports from the same person
notices.detail: A pattern of unsubstantiated reports from one source is harassment, not genuine concern.

notices.signal: The reports coincide with custody disputes or conflict
notices.detail: Reports that arrive right before court dates or during disagreements are tactical, not protective.

notices.signal: Each report is unfounded but they keep coming
notices.detail: The perpetrator knows the reports won't lead to action — the check itself is the weapon.

actions.action: Document every welfare check
actions.detail: Record dates, times, what was reported, by whom, and the outcome. This pattern is your evidence.

actions.action: Ask responding officers to note the pattern in their records
actions.detail: Police can flag repeated unsubstantiated reports from the same complainant.

actions.action: Seek legal advice about vexatious reporting
actions.detail: Repeatedly making false or malicious reports may itself be an offence and can be raised in family court.

techniques.name: Legal System Abuse / Litigation Abuse
techniques.description: Using repeated court applications, vexatious claims, subpoenas, discovery requests, or procedural motions as financial and psychological weapons. Filing and withdrawing AVOs, repeated custody variations, dragging out property settlements, issuing subpoenas to employers or therapists. Each action costs the victim money and emotional energy. The legal system itself becomes the abuse tool. Sometimes called 'systems abuse' or 'paper abuse.'
techniques.public_title: Someone is using the legal system as a weapon against you
techniques.public_summary: They keep filing court applications, making legal threats, demanding documents, and dragging out proceedings. Each one costs you money, time, and emotional energy — and they know it. The legal process itself has become the abuse.

notices.signal: Court applications that seem designed to cause you stress rather than achieve an outcome
notices.detail: Applications that are withdrawn before hearing, filed right before holidays, or repeat issues already resolved.

notices.signal: Legal costs are escalating beyond what the issues warrant
notices.detail: Spending $50,000 fighting over $5,000 of property isn't about the property.

notices.signal: Every attempt at resolution is met with new demands or applications
notices.detail: The goal isn't resolution — it's continuation. The process is the punishment.

notices.signal: Subpoenas or discovery requests targeting your support network
notices.detail: Subpoenaing your therapist's notes, your employer's records, or your friends' messages — using legal process to invade your life.

actions.action: Document the pattern, not just individual applications
actions.detail: Courts respond to patterns. A timeline of 15 applications in 12 months tells a story that individual responses don't.

actions.action: Ask your lawyer about vexatious litigant provisions
actions.detail: Australian courts can declare someone a vexatious litigant, requiring leave before filing further applications.

actions.action: Seek a family violence-informed lawyer
actions.detail: Not all family lawyers understand systems abuse. Find one who recognises litigation as a form of control.

actions.action: Access legal aid or pro bono services if costs are unsustainable
actions.detail: Financial exhaustion is part of the strategy. Legal aid, community legal centres, and Women's Legal Services can help.

techniques.name: Post-Separation App Weaponisation
techniques.description: Exploiting court-mandated communication apps (OurFamilyWizard, AppClose, Talking Parents) for microcontrol, excessive documentation demands, or manipulative communication that technically complies with court orders but is designed to exhaust and control. Weaponising the 'paper trail' feature to create false evidence of the other parent's non-compliance. The apps meant to protect victims become tools of abuse.
techniques.public_title: The co-parenting app has become another tool of control
techniques.public_summary: The court-ordered communication app was supposed to make things safer, but they're using it to send dozens of messages a day, demand immediate responses, document everything you do, and create a record that makes you look non-compliant. The app that was meant to protect you has become another weapon.

notices.signal: Dozens of messages a day about trivial matters
notices.detail: Asking what the children ate for breakfast, requesting photos of homework, demanding updates on every activity — the volume is the weapon.

notices.signal: Every message is carefully worded to sound reasonable in isolation
notices.detail: Each individual message looks fine. It's the pattern — the volume, the demands, the tone — that constitutes abuse.

notices.signal: They screenshot and use your response times against you
notices.detail: 'She took 4 hours to respond about pickup' — using the app's documentation features to build a false narrative.

notices.signal: You feel anxious every time you get a notification from the app
notices.detail: If a communication tool causes dread, it's not functioning as intended.

actions.action: Set boundaries on response times
actions.detail: You don't need to respond immediately to every message. Set a reasonable schedule (e.g., checking the app twice daily) and document it.

actions.action: Keep responses brief and factual
actions.detail: Don't engage with provocative messages. 'Noted' or 'Confirmed' are complete responses.

actions.action: Document the pattern for your lawyer
actions.detail: Screenshot the volume — 47 messages in one day about lunch choices is evidence of harassment, not co-parenting.

actions.action: Raise it with the court
actions.detail: Courts are increasingly aware of app weaponisation. The pattern of misuse can be raised and orders can be amended.
